questions.Subject: Biology
questions.Question: Which of the following characteristics distinguishes living organisms from non-living things?
questions.OptionA: Ability to undergo metabolic activities and reproduce
questions.OptionB: Presence of definite geometrical crystalline structures
questions.OptionC: Ability to expand solely in response to thermal heating
questions.OptionD: Inability to alter shape or chemical composition
questions.Option_a: Ability to undergo metabolic activities and reproduce
questions.Option_b: Presence of definite geometrical crystalline structures
questions.Option_c: Ability to expand solely in response to thermal heating
questions.Option_d: Inability to alter shape or chemical composition
questions.Explanation: Living organisms carry out life processes such as metabolism, respiration, growth, irritability, and reproduction, which are absent in non-living matter.

questions.Subject: Biology
questions.Question: Viruses are described as living entities only when they
questions.OptionA: are crystallized and stored in a glass test tube
questions.OptionB: are inside the living cells of a host organism
questions.OptionC: are suspended in distilled sterile water
questions.OptionD: undergo binary fission on an agar culture medium
questions.Option_a: are crystallized and stored in a glass test tube
questions.Option_b: are inside the living cells of a host organism
questions.Option_c: are suspended in distilled sterile water
questions.Option_d: undergo binary fission on an agar culture medium
questions.Explanation: Viruses are obligate intracellular parasites that display living characteristics (such as replication) only inside living host cells; outside a host, they behave like non-living crystals.

questions.Subject: Biology
questions.Question: The irreversible increase in size, mass, and dry weight of an organism is termed
questions.Explanation: Growth in biology is defined as an irreversible, permanent increase in the size, dry biomass, and complexity of an organism.

questions.Subject: Biology
questions.Question: The ability of living organisms to detect and respond appropriately to stimuli in their environment is known as
questions.Explanation: Irritability (sensitivity) is the capacity to perceive external or internal environmental stimuli and mount a coordinated response.

questions.Subject: Biology
questions.Question: Which of the following is a non-living characteristic displayed by viruses?
questions.OptionA: Ability to be crystallized and stored indefinitely without metabolizing
questions.OptionB: Possession of genetic material in the form of DNA or RNA
questions.OptionC: Ability to undergo genetic mutation and evolution
questions.OptionD: Inducing infected host cells to produce viral proteins
questions.Option_a: Ability to be crystallized and stored indefinitely without metabolizing
questions.Option_b: Possession of genetic material in the form of DNA or RNA
questions.Option_c: Ability to undergo genetic mutation and evolution
questions.Option_d: Inducing infected host cells to produce viral proteins
questions.Explanation: Viruses can be crystallized and precipitated like chemical salts, displaying no independent metabolic respiration or excretion.

questions.Subject: Biology
questions.Question: Metabolism in living organisms consists of two opposing processes known as
questions.Explanation: Metabolism comprises constructive, energy-consuming reactions (anabolism) and destructive, energy-releasing breakdown reactions (catabolism).

questions.Subject: Biology
questions.Question: Which of the following statements about excretion in living organisms is correct?
questions.OptionA: It is the discharge of undigested food matter through the anus (egestion)
questions.OptionB: It occurs only in warm-blooded terrestrial vertebrates
questions.OptionC: It is the removal of toxic and unwanted metabolic waste products from the body
questions.OptionD: It is identical to the mechanical ventilation of air in the lungs
questions.Option_a: It is the discharge of undigested food matter through the anus (egestion)
questions.Option_b: It occurs only in warm-blooded terrestrial vertebrates
questions.Option_c: It is the removal of toxic and unwanted metabolic waste products from the body
questions.Option_d: It is identical to the mechanical ventilation of air in the lungs
questions.Explanation: Excretion is strictly the elimination of toxic end-products of cellular metabolism (such as urea, carbon dioxide, and uric acid), unlike egestion which eliminates undigested food.

questions.Subject: Biology
questions.Question: Locomotion in animals differs from movement in plants because locomotion
questions.OptionA: is solely driven by external gravitational forces
questions.OptionB: occurs without the expenditure of cellular metabolic energy
questions.OptionC: is limited to localized curvature responses of vegetative stems
questions.OptionD: involves the movement of the entire organism from one place to another
questions.Option_a: is solely driven by external gravitational forces
questions.Option_b: occurs without the expenditure of cellular metabolic energy
questions.Option_c: is limited to localized curvature responses of vegetative stems
questions.Option_d: involves the movement of the entire organism from one place to another
questions.Explanation: Locomotion is the displacement of the whole body from one geographical position to another, typical of animals, whereas plants mainly exhibit movement of parts.

questions.Subject: Biology
questions.Question: Which of the following processes represents an anabolic metabolic pathway in living systems?
questions.OptionA: Synthesis of glucose from carbon dioxide and water during photosynthesis
questions.OptionB: Breakdown of glycogen into glucose molecules in the liver
questions.OptionC: Hydrolysis of dietary proteins into amino acids in the stomach
questions.OptionD: Oxidative breakdown of pyruvate into carbon dioxide in mitochondria
questions.Option_a: Synthesis of glucose from carbon dioxide and water during photosynthesis
questions.Option_b: Breakdown of glycogen into glucose molecules in the liver
questions.Option_c: Hydrolysis of dietary proteins into amino acids in the stomach
questions.Option_d: Oxidative breakdown of pyruvate into carbon dioxide in mitochondria
questions.Explanation: Anabolism involves building complex macromolecules from simpler precursors, exemplified by the photosynthetic synthesis of hexose sugars.

questions.Subject: Biology
questions.Question: Homeostasis is the biological process whereby an organism
questions.OptionA: increases its rate of mutation to resist pathogenic bacteria
questions.OptionB: maintains a relatively constant internal physiological environment
questions.OptionC: replaces dead somatic cells through meiotic gamete production
questions.OptionD: absorbs mineral salts against a steep chemical concentration gradient
questions.Option_a: increases its rate of mutation to resist pathogenic bacteria
questions.Option_b: maintains a relatively constant internal physiological environment
questions.Option_c: replaces dead somatic cells through meiotic gamete production
questions.Option_d: absorbs mineral salts against a steep chemical concentration gradient
questions.Explanation: Homeostasis is the regulation and maintenance of stable internal conditions (e.g. body temperature, blood pH, glucose concentration) despite external fluctuations.

questions.Subject: Biology
questions.Question: Which of the following is an example of a catabolic reaction in animal cells?
questions.OptionA: Condensation of amino acids to form polypeptide enzyme chains
questions.OptionB: Formation of triglycerides from fatty acids and glycerol
questions.OptionC: Cellular respiration breaking down glucose into carbon dioxide, water, and ATP
questions.OptionD: Synthesis of ribonucleic acid from ribonucleotides
questions.Option_a: Condensation of amino acids to form polypeptide enzyme chains
questions.Option_b: Formation of triglycerides from fatty acids and glycerol
questions.Option_c: Cellular respiration breaking down glucose into carbon dioxide, water, and ATP
questions.Option_d: Synthesis of ribonucleic acid from ribonucleotides
questions.Explanation: Cellular respiration is a catabolic process wherein nutrient molecules are oxidized and broken down to release energy in the form of ATP.

questions.Subject: Biology
questions.Question: The release of energy in living cells through the breakdown of organic substrates is termed
questions.Explanation: Cellular respiration is the biochemical oxidation of organic nutrients inside cells to yield biological energy (ATP).

questions.Subject: Biology
questions.Question: Which feature confirms that Euglena viridis possesses both plant and animal characteristics?
questions.OptionA: Presence of chloroplasts for autotrophy and a gullet/flagellum for motility and heterotrophy
questions.OptionB: Presence of a rigid cellulose cell wall and an endoskeleton
questions.OptionC: Absence of a nucleus and possession of circular plasmid DNA
questions.OptionD: Ability to produce meiotic endospores during dry seasons
questions.Option_a: Presence of chloroplasts for autotrophy and a gullet/flagellum for motility and heterotrophy
questions.Option_b: Presence of a rigid cellulose cell wall and an endoskeleton
questions.Option_c: Absence of a nucleus and possession of circular plasmid DNA
questions.Option_d: Ability to produce meiotic endospores during dry seasons
questions.Explanation: Euglena is mixotrophic: it contains chloroplasts for photosynthesis (plant-like) and possesses a flagellum, eyespot, and gullet for feeding and locomotion (animal-like).

questions.Subject: Biology
questions.Question: Which of the following environmental factors serves as a chemical stimulus triggering chemotaxis in motile bacteria?
questions.OptionA: Fluctuations in atmospheric barometric air pressure
questions.OptionB: Concentration gradient of glucose or attractant amino acids
questions.OptionD: The electrostatic friction of air molecules
questions.Option_a: Fluctuations in atmospheric barometric air pressure
questions.Option_b: Concentration gradient of glucose or attractant amino acids
questions.Option_d: The electrostatic friction of air molecules
questions.Explanation: Chemotaxis is the directed directional movement of motile cells or organisms toward or away from specific chemical substances.

questions.Subject: Biology
questions.Question: Which of the following best explains why reproduction is necessary for living organisms?
questions.OptionA: It increases the dry weight of an individual adult organism
questions.OptionB: It eliminates toxic nitrogenous metabolic wastes from the body
questions.OptionC: It ensures the continuity of the species and prevents biological extinction
questions.OptionD: It provides energy needed for active transport across cell membranes
questions.Option_a: It increases the dry weight of an individual adult organism
questions.Option_b: It eliminates toxic nitrogenous metabolic wastes from the body
questions.Option_c: It ensures the continuity of the species and prevents biological extinction
questions.Option_d: It provides energy needed for active transport across cell membranes
questions.Explanation: Reproduction allows organisms to produce viable offspring, thereby propagating genetic traits and guaranteeing the survival of the species over generations.

questions.Subject: Biology
questions.Question: A stone increases in size when sediment accumulates on its surface. This differs from biological growth because the stone grows by
questions.OptionB: meiotic duplication of constituent crystalline mineral atoms
questions.OptionC: photosynthetic assimilation of atmospheric carbon compounds
questions.OptionD: accretion (external addition of matter), whereas organisms grow by internal cell division and assimilation
questions.Option_b: meiotic duplication of constituent crystalline mineral atoms
questions.Option_c: photosynthetic assimilation of atmospheric carbon compounds
questions.Option_d: accretion (external addition of matter), whereas organisms grow by internal cell division and assimilation
questions.Explanation: Non-living matter increases in size externally by accretion of external layers, whereas living organisms grow internally (by intussusception) through cell division and metabolic assimilation.

questions.Subject: Biology
questions.Question: Adaptation in living organisms is best described as
questions.OptionA: any structural, physiological, or behavioural trait that improves survival and reproductive success in a given habitat
questions.OptionB: the complete cessation of all cellular metabolic reactions during dormancy
questions.OptionC: the loss of unnecessary genetic material during meiotic crossing over
questions.OptionD: an involuntary reflex response to a sudden loud auditory sound
questions.Option_a: any structural, physiological, or behavioural trait that improves survival and reproductive success in a given habitat
questions.Option_b: the complete cessation of all cellular metabolic reactions during dormancy
questions.Option_c: the loss of unnecessary genetic material during meiotic crossing over
questions.Option_d: an involuntary reflex response to a sudden loud auditory sound
questions.Explanation: An adaptation is an inherited anatomical, physiological, or behavioral modification that fits an organism to thrive and reproduce in its specific ecological niche.

questions.Subject: Biology
questions.Question: Which of the following organelles is known as the 'powerhouse of the cell' due to its role in ATP synthesis?
questions.Explanation: Mitochondria generate the majority of cellular chemical energy in the form of ATP via aerobic cellular respiration and the Krebs cycle.

questions.Subject: Biology
questions.Question: Which of the following structures is present in typical plant cells but absent in animal cells?
questions.Explanation: Plant cells possess a rigid outer cellulose cell wall, large central vacuoles, and photosynthetic chloroplasts, which are absent in animal cells.

questions.Subject: Biology
questions.Question: The site of protein synthesis in both eukaryotic and prokaryotic cells is the
questions.Explanation: Ribosomes are granular ribonucleoprotein structures responsible for translating mRNA codons into polypeptide chains during protein synthesis.

questions.Subject: Biology
questions.Question: Which cellular organelle contains powerful hydrolytic enzymes that break down worn-out cell parts and foreign pathogens?
questions.Explanation: Lysosomes contain acid hydrolases capable of digesting cellular macromolecules, worn-out organelles (autophagy), and engulfed bacteria.

questions.Subject: Biology
questions.Question: The fluid mosaic model of the plasma membrane describes it as a bilayer of
questions.OptionA: rigid cellulose fibers impregnated with pectin
questions.OptionB: phospholipids with embedded and peripheral proteins
questions.OptionC: solid protein sheets enclosing liquid triglycerides
questions.Option_a: rigid cellulose fibers impregnated with pectin
questions.Option_b: phospholipids with embedded and peripheral proteins
questions.Option_c: solid protein sheets enclosing liquid triglycerides
questions.Explanation: Singer and Nicolson's fluid mosaic model depicts the cell membrane as a viscous lipid bilayer of amphipathic phospholipids with mobile embedded proteins.

questions.Subject: Biology
questions.Question: Under a light microscope, if an eyepiece lens has a magnification of x10 and the objective lens has a magnification of x40, what is the total magnification?
questions.Explanation: Total magnification = Eyepiece magnification × Objective lens magnification = 10 × 40 = x400.

questions.Subject: Biology
questions.Question: Which organelle is responsible for packaging, modifying, and sorting proteins for secretion?
questions.Explanation: The Golgi apparatus modifies proteins delivered from the rough ER, packages them into secretory vesicles, and sorts them for cellular export or lysosomes.

questions.Subject: Biology
questions.Question: Prokaryotic cells differ from eukaryotic cells primarily because prokaryotes
questions.OptionA: lack a membrane-bound nucleus and membrane-bound organelles
questions.OptionB: do not possess genetic material or nucleic acids
questions.OptionC: cannot synthesize proteins or biological enzymes
questions.Option_a: lack a membrane-bound nucleus and membrane-bound organelles
questions.Option_b: do not possess genetic material or nucleic acids
questions.Option_c: cannot synthesize proteins or biological enzymes
questions.Explanation: Prokaryotes (e.g. bacteria) lack a distinct membrane-enclosed nucleus (possessing a naked nucleoid) and membrane-bound organelles.

questions.Subject: Biology
questions.Question: The rough endoplasmic reticulum (RER) appears 'rough' under an electron microscope because its outer surface is studded with
questions.Explanation: Rough endoplasmic reticulum is lined with ribosomes actively engaged in synthesizing proteins destined for secretion or membrane insertion.

questions.Subject: Biology
questions.Question: Which organelle in plant cells contains the green pigment chlorophyll necessary for trapping sunlight during photosynthesis?
questions.Explanation: Chloroplasts are double-membrane plastids containing thylakoids and stroma rich in chlorophyll that capture light energy for photosynthesis.

questions.Subject: Biology
questions.Question: Centrioles are specialized organelles that play an active role in animal cells during
questions.OptionB: transcription of messenger RNA in the nucleoplasm
questions.OptionC: translocation of sugars across phloem sieve tubes
questions.OptionD: spindle fiber formation during cell division
questions.Option_b: transcription of messenger RNA in the nucleoplasm
questions.Option_c: translocation of sugars across phloem sieve tubes
questions.Option_d: spindle fiber formation during cell division
questions.Explanation: Centrioles organize the mitotic spindle fibers that separate chromosomes during mitosis and meiosis in animal cells.

questions.Subject: Biology
questions.Question: Which chemical stain is commonly used to stain onion epidermal cells for examination under a light microscope?
questions.Explanation: Iodine solution stains starch granules and highlights cell walls and nuclei, making plant cell structures distinct under the microscope.

questions.Subject: Biology
questions.Question: The selectively permeable nature of the cell membrane means that it
questions.OptionA: permits all solutes to diffuse freely without restriction
questions.OptionB: allows certain substances to pass through while preventing others
questions.OptionC: is completely impermeable to water and gaseous molecules
questions.OptionD: only allows the passage of solid mineral crystals
questions.Option_a: permits all solutes to diffuse freely without restriction
questions.Option_b: allows certain substances to pass through while preventing others
questions.Option_c: is completely impermeable to water and gaseous molecules
questions.Option_d: only allows the passage of solid mineral crystals
questions.Explanation: Selective (differential) permeability allows the cell membrane to regulate internal composition by controlling which ions and molecules cross.

questions.Subject: Biology
questions.Question: What is the function of the nucleolus located inside the cell nucleus?
questions.OptionA: Oxidative breakdown of pyruvate into acetyl coenzyme A
questions.OptionB: Detoxification of lipid-soluble drugs and toxic substances
questions.OptionC: Synthesis and assembly of ribosomal RNA (rRNA) and ribosome subunits
questions.OptionD: Storage of starch grains and glycogen granules
questions.Option_a: Oxidative breakdown of pyruvate into acetyl coenzyme A
questions.Option_b: Detoxification of lipid-soluble drugs and toxic substances
questions.Option_c: Synthesis and assembly of ribosomal RNA (rRNA) and ribosome subunits
questions.Option_d: Storage of starch grains and glycogen granules
questions.Explanation: The nucleolus is the dense nuclear region where ribosomal RNA transcription and pre-ribosomal subunit assembly take place.

questions.Subject: Biology
questions.Question: The resolution of an electron microscope is far superior to that of a light microscope because
questions.OptionA: electron microscopes use thick glass convex lenses
questions.OptionB: light waves travel faster through biological specimens than electrons
questions.OptionC: electron microscopes can examine live specimens in natural wet conditions
questions.OptionD: the wavelength of an electron beam is much shorter than the wavelength of visible light
questions.Option_a: electron microscopes use thick glass convex lenses
questions.Option_b: light waves travel faster through biological specimens than electrons
questions.Option_c: electron microscopes can examine live specimens in natural wet conditions
questions.Option_d: the wavelength of an electron beam is much shorter than the wavelength of visible light
questions.Explanation: Resolution is inversely proportional to wavelength. The extremely short wavelength of high-energy electron beams enables resolving sub-nanometer cellular ultrastructure.

questions.Subject: Biology
questions.Question: Which of the following structures in bacterial cells provides protection against phagocytosis and desiccation?
questions.Explanation: The bacterial capsule is an external polysaccharide layer that protects pathogenic bacteria from engulfment by host white blood cells and dehydration.

questions.Subject: Biology
questions.Question: In mature plant cells, the large central vacuole is enveloped by a selectively permeable membrane called the
questions.Explanation: The tonoplast is the specialized cytoplasmic membrane bounding the central vacuole in plant cells, maintaining turgor pressure.

questions.Subject: Biology
questions.Question: Which of the following represents the correct hierarchical order of biological organization from simplest to most complex?
questions.Explanation: Biological organization ascends from the basic functional unit (cell) to collections of similar cells (tissue), functional units (organ), organ groups (system), and the whole organism.

questions.Subject: Biology
questions.Question: Which of the following organisms exists and functions at the single cell level of organization?
questions.Explanation: Amoeba is a unicellular protozoan that performs all vital physiological functions (nutrition, respiration, excretion, reproduction) within a single cell.

questions.Subject: Biology
questions.Question: An example of a colonial organism where individual cells live in a coordinated matrix is
questions.Explanation: Volvox forms spherical colonies of hundreds of biflagellated cells interconnected by cytoplasmic strands, functioning as an integrated colonial entity.

questions.Subject: Biology
questions.Question: Which of the following organisms represents a filamentous level of organization?
questions.Explanation: Spirogyra is a green alga composed of unbranched, linear filaments of identical cells arranged end-to-end.

questions.Subject: Biology
questions.Question: A group of specialized cells of similar structure performing a specific common function in a multicellular organism is called a
questions.Explanation: A tissue is an assemblage of structurally similar cells and associated intercellular matrix coordinated to perform a specialized physiological function.

questions.Subject: Biology
questions.Question: Which of the following is an example of an animal tissue?
questions.Explanation: Epithelium is a fundamental animal tissue that covers body surfaces and cavities. The stomach and heart are organs, while the digestive tract is a system.

questions.Subject: Biology
questions.Question: In higher plants, the leaf is correctly classified as an
questions.Explanation: A leaf is a plant organ composed of multiple tissues (epidermal, palisade mesophyll, spongy mesophyll, xylem, phloem) working together for photosynthesis.

questions.Subject: Biology
questions.Question: An advantage of multicellularity and division of labour among specialized cells is that it
questions.OptionA: eliminates the biological requirement for cellular respiration
questions.OptionB: increases the efficiency and adaptability of the organism in exploiting diverse ecological niches
questions.OptionC: allows all constituent cells to divide at the identical mitotic velocity
questions.OptionD: enables the organism to survive without absorbing mineral salts
questions.Option_a: eliminates the biological requirement for cellular respiration
questions.Option_b: increases the efficiency and adaptability of the organism in exploiting diverse ecological niches
questions.Option_c: allows all constituent cells to divide at the identical mitotic velocity
questions.Option_d: enables the organism to survive without absorbing mineral salts
questions.Explanation: Cellular differentiation and specialization allow multicellular organisms to perform complex tasks efficiently and maintain homeostasis across varied habitats.

questions.Subject: Biology
questions.Question: Which of the following organisms exhibits the tissue level of organization without distinct organ systems?
questions.Explanation: Coelenterates (cnidarians) such as Hydra are diploblastic organisms possessing specialized tissues (ectoderm and endoderm) but lacking true organs and organ systems.

questions.Subject: Biology
questions.Question: Which of the following is a plant tissue responsible for the translocation of manufactured organic food substances?
questions.Explanation: Phloem tissue (comprising sieve tubes and companion cells) transports synthesized sucrose from source leaves to sink tissues.

questions.Subject: Biology
questions.Question: The heart, blood vessels, and blood collectively constitute which level of biological organization?
questions.Explanation: The heart and vascular network operate together to deliver transport functions, forming the cardiovascular (circulatory) organ system.

questions.Subject: Biology
questions.Question: Which of the following is a plant tissue specialized for providing mechanical support and flexibility in young growing stems?
questions.Explanation: Collenchyma consists of elongated living cells with unevenly thickened cellulosic primary walls, providing pliable mechanical support to young stems and petioles.

questions.Subject: Biology
questions.Question: A major disadvantage of high cellular specialization in complex multicellular organisms is that
questions.OptionA: the organism cannot grow larger than two millimeters in diameter
questions.OptionB: energy expenditure during cellular respiration decreases to zero
questions.OptionC: individual specialized cells become dependent on others and cannot survive in isolation
questions.OptionD: the organism loses the ability to respond to external sensory stimuli
questions.Option_a: the organism cannot grow larger than two millimeters in diameter
questions.Option_b: energy expenditure during cellular respiration decreases to zero
questions.Option_c: individual specialized cells become dependent on others and cannot survive in isolation
questions.Option_d: the organism loses the ability to respond to external sensory stimuli
questions.Explanation: Specialized somatic cells lose autonomy; if one vital organ system fails (e.g. heart or kidney failure), the entire organism is endangered.

questions.Subject: Biology
questions.Question: Which of the following cell types in human blood is specialized for the transport of oxygen?
questions.Explanation: Erythrocytes are biconcave, enucleated cells packed with iron-containing hemoglobin molecules dedicated to oxygen transport.

questions.Subject: Biology
questions.Question: The kidney is an example of an organ because it
questions.OptionA: consists of different tissues working together to excrete wastes and maintain osmoregulation
questions.OptionB: is made up of a single giant multinucleated cell
questions.OptionC: belongs to the colonial level of biological organization
questions.OptionD: operates completely independently of the nervous and circulatory systems
questions.Option_a: consists of different tissues working together to excrete wastes and maintain osmoregulation
questions.Option_b: is made up of a single giant multinucleated cell
questions.Option_c: belongs to the colonial level of biological organization
questions.Option_d: operates completely independently of the nervous and circulatory systems
questions.Explanation: The kidney is an organ containing connective, vascular, nervous, and specialized nephron epithelial tissues coordinated for excretion and fluid balance.

questions.Subject: Biology
questions.Question: Paramecium caudatum achieves osmoregulation through which specialized unicellular organelle?
questions.Explanation: The contractile vacuole collects excess hypotonic water diffusing into the cytoplasm and periodically pulsates to expel it, maintaining osmotic equilibrium.

questions.Subject: Biology
questions.Question: Which of the following represents an organ system in flowering plants?
questions.OptionA: Palisade mesophyll layer inside a foliage leaf
questions.OptionB: Individual bordered pit of a xylem tracheid vessel
questions.OptionC: Shoot system (comprising stems, leaves, buds, and flowers)
questions.OptionD: Guard cell pair flanking a stomatal pore
questions.Option_a: Palisade mesophyll layer inside a foliage leaf
questions.Option_b: Individual bordered pit of a xylem tracheid vessel
questions.Option_c: Shoot system (comprising stems, leaves, buds, and flowers)
questions.Option_d: Guard cell pair flanking a stomatal pore
questions.Explanation: The shoot system is a macroscopic plant organ system consisting of coordinated organs (stems, foliage leaves, floral buds) dedicated to photosynthesis, support, and reproduction.

questions.Subject: Biology
questions.Question: The type of cell division that produces two daughter cells with an identical chromosome number as the parent cell is called
questions.Explanation: Mitosis is equational cell division where one diploid (2n) or haploid (n) parent cell divides to produce two genetically identical daughter cells.

questions.Subject: Biology
questions.Question: In humans, somatic body cells contain 46 chromosomes. How many chromosomes will each daughter cell possess after undergoing mitosis?
questions.Explanation: Mitosis preserves the chromosome number; a human diploid somatic cell (46 chromosomes) produces two daughter cells each containing exactly 46 chromosomes.

questions.Subject: Biology
questions.Question: During which stage of mitosis do sister chromatids separate and migrate toward opposite poles of the cell?
questions.Explanation: During anaphase, centromeres split and spindle fibers pull the separated sister chromatids (now individual daughter chromosomes) toward opposite spindle poles.

questions.Subject: Biology
questions.Question: At which phase of mitosis do chromosomes align singly along the equatorial plane of the spindle apparatus?
questions.Explanation: In metaphase, chromosomes reach maximum condensation and align along the cell's equatorial metaphase plate attached to spindle fibers by their kinetochores.

questions.Subject: Biology
questions.Question: Meiosis is also known as reduction division because it
questions.OptionA: reduces the size of daughter cells by ninety percent
questions.OptionB: decreases the cellular metabolic rate during nuclear division
questions.OptionC: destroys half of the mitochondria in each daughter cell
questions.OptionD: halves the diploid chromosome number (2n) to a haploid number (n) in resulting gametes
questions.Option_a: reduces the size of daughter cells by ninety percent
questions.Option_b: decreases the cellular metabolic rate during nuclear division
questions.Option_c: destroys half of the mitochondria in each daughter cell
questions.Option_d: halves the diploid chromosome number (2n) to a haploid number (n) in resulting gametes
questions.Explanation: Meiosis involves two successive nuclear divisions following one round of replication, halving the chromosome complement from diploid (2n) to haploid (n).

questions.Subject: Biology
questions.Question: In which human reproductive organs does meiosis take place to produce haploid gametes?
questions.Explanation: Meiosis (gametogenesis) occurs specifically in the germline cells of the gonads: the testes (spermatogenesis) and ovaries (oogenesis).

questions.Subject: Biology
questions.Question: The exchange of genetic material between non-sister chromatids of homologous chromosomes during prophase I of meiosis is termed
questions.Explanation: Crossing over occurs at chiasmata during pachytene of prophase I, generating novel allele combinations that introduce genetic variation.

questions.Subject: Biology
questions.Question: How many haploid daughter cells are produced at the completion of a single meiotic division cycle?
questions.Explanation: Meiosis consists of Meiosis I and Meiosis II, culminating in the production of four genetically distinct haploid (n) daughter cells (gametes or spores).

questions.Subject: Biology
questions.Question: Which of the following biological roles is accomplished by mitotic cell division in multicellular organisms?
questions.OptionA: Production of haploid spermatozoa and ova
questions.OptionB: Halving chromosome numbers prior to fertilization
questions.OptionC: Promoting crossing over and extensive genetic variability
questions.OptionD: Tissue growth, repair of damaged cells, and asexual reproduction
questions.Option_a: Production of haploid spermatozoa and ova
questions.Option_b: Halving chromosome numbers prior to fertilization
questions.Option_c: Promoting crossing over and extensive genetic variability
questions.Option_d: Tissue growth, repair of damaged cells, and asexual reproduction
questions.Explanation: Mitosis drives organismal growth, replaces worn-out cells (tissue repair), and serves as the vehicle for vegetative/asexual reproduction.

questions.Subject: Biology
questions.Question: The period of the cell cycle between successive cell divisions when DNA replication occurs is called
questions.Explanation: Interphase (comprising G1, S, and G2 phases) is the metabolically active period where cell growth and chromosome DNA replication (S phase) occur.

questions.Subject: Biology
questions.Question: Cytokinesis in animal cells differs from cytokinesis in plant cells because plant cells divide by
questions.OptionA: pinching inward to form a cleavage furrow of microfilaments
questions.OptionB: forming a cell plate across the equator that develops into a new cell wall
questions.OptionC: undergoing binary fission of the outer cellulose wall
questions.OptionD: budding small daughter vacuoles from the nuclear membrane
questions.Option_a: pinching inward to form a cleavage furrow of microfilaments
questions.Option_b: forming a cell plate across the equator that develops into a new cell wall
questions.Option_c: undergoing binary fission of the outer cellulose wall
questions.Option_d: budding small daughter vacuoles from the nuclear membrane
questions.Explanation: Plant cells are bounded by rigid cell walls and cannot form cleavage furrows; instead, Golgi vesicles coalesce at the equator to assemble a cell plate.

questions.Subject: Biology
questions.Question: During which phase of meiotic prophase I do homologous chromosomes pair up gene-for-gene in a process called synapsis?
questions.Explanation: Synapsis occurs during the zygotene substage of prophase I, forming bivalents (tetrads) mediated by the synaptonemal complex.

questions.Subject: Biology
questions.Question: The failure of homologous chromosomes or sister chromatids to separate properly during cell division is called
questions.Explanation: Non-disjunction leads to aneuploidy (abnormal chromosome numbers in daughter cells), as seen in Down syndrome (Trisomy 21).

questions.Subject: Biology
questions.Question: What is the biological significance of meiosis in sexually reproducing species?
questions.OptionA: It maintains a constant species chromosome number across generations and introduces genetic diversity
questions.OptionB: It produces genetically identical clones of parent organisms
questions.OptionC: It increases the somatic chromosome count exponentially every generation
questions.OptionD: It eliminates the necessity of fertilization between male and female gametes
questions.Option_a: It maintains a constant species chromosome number across generations and introduces genetic diversity
questions.Option_b: It produces genetically identical clones of parent organisms
questions.Option_c: It increases the somatic chromosome count exponentially every generation
questions.Option_d: It eliminates the necessity of fertilization between male and female gametes
questions.Explanation: By halving the chromosome number in gametes, meiosis prevents doubling of chromosomes at fertilization, while crossing over fuels genetic variation.

questions.Subject: Biology
questions.Question: Cancer is biologically defined as a disease caused by
questions.OptionA: failure of meiotic gametes to undergo fertilization
questions.OptionB: uncontrolled, abnormal mitotic division and proliferation of cells
questions.OptionC: excessive accumulation of glycogen in striated muscle tissues
questions.OptionD: complete cessation of DNA replication during interphase
questions.Option_a: failure of meiotic gametes to undergo fertilization
questions.Option_b: uncontrolled, abnormal mitotic division and proliferation of cells
questions.Option_c: excessive accumulation of glycogen in striated muscle tissues
questions.Option_d: complete cessation of DNA replication during interphase
questions.Explanation: Cancer arises when mutations disrupt cell cycle checkpoints, leading to unrestrained, malignant mitotic proliferation that invades tissues.

questions.Subject: Biology
questions.Question: In flowering plants, meiosis directly leads to the formation of
questions.OptionD: cuticle layers over the upper foliage epidermis
questions.Option_d: cuticle layers over the upper foliage epidermis
questions.Explanation: Meiosis in angiosperms occurs in anther sporangia (microsporogenesis) and ovules (megasporogenesis) to produce haploid spores.

questions.Subject: Biology
questions.Question: The scientific system of naming organisms using a two-part Latinized name was introduced by
questions.Explanation: Swedish botanist Carl Linnaeus devised the binomial nomenclature system in the 18th century, assigning every species a genus and species name.

questions.Subject: Biology
questions.Question: Which of the following taxonomic ranks is the most basic, fundamental unit of biological classification?
questions.Explanation: The species is the fundamental taxonomic unit, comprising individuals capable of interbreeding in nature to produce fertile offspring.

questions.Subject: Biology
questions.Question: Which of the following represents the correct hierarchical sequence of taxonomic classification from highest to lowest?
questions.OptionA: Kingdom → Class → Phylum → Family → Order → Genus → Species

questions.OptionC: Phylum → Kingdom → Class → Order → Genus → Family → Species

questions.Option_d: Kingdom → Phylum → Class → Order → Family → Genus → Species
questions.Explanation: The standard taxonomic hierarchy descends from Kingdom down through Phylum, Class, Order, Family, Genus, to Species.

questions.Subject: Biology
questions.Question: In Whittaker's five-kingdom classification scheme, unicellular organisms lacking a membrane-bound nucleus are placed in Kingdom
questions.Explanation: Kingdom Monera comprises all prokaryotes (eubacteria and cyanobacteria) characterized by the absence of a membrane-enclosed nucleus.

questions.Subject: Biology
questions.Question: Which of the following plant groups lacks true roots, stems, leaves, and vascular tissues (xylem and phloem)?
questions.Explanation: Bryophytes are non-vascular, thalloid land plants that lack lignified conducting tissues (xylem and phloem) and true roots.

questions.Subject: Biology

questions.OptionD: true vascular bundles (xylem and phloem) and true roots, stems, and leaves

questions.Option_d: true vascular bundles (xylem and phloem) and true roots, stems, and leaves

questions.Subject: Biology
questions.Question: Which of the following is a defining characteristic of members of the Phylum Arthropoda?

questions.Option_d: A closed circulatory system and chaetae on every segment

questions.Subject: Biology
questions.Question: To which class of arthropods do spiders, scorpions, and ticks belong?
questions.Explanation: Arachnids possess two main body regions (cephalothorax and abdomen), four pairs of walking legs, and lack antennae and wings.

questions.Subject: Biology
questions.Question: Which vertebrate class is characterized by having dry scaly skin, laying cleidoic (amniotic) eggs on land, and being poikilothermic?
questions.Explanation: Reptiles have keratinized epidermal scales, breathe via lungs, are ectothermic (poikilothermic), and produce leathery shelled amniotic eggs.

questions.Option_d: can switch between autotrophic photosynthesis and animal predation
questions.Explanation: Amphibians (e.g. toads, frogs) undergo metamorphosis: aquatic larvae breathe with gills, while semi-terrestrial adults breathe via lungs and moist skin.

questions.Subject: Biology
questions.Question: Mammals are distinguished from all other vertebrate classes by the presence of
questions.OptionA: a four-chambered heart and homoiothermic body temperature

questions.Subject: Biology
questions.Question: Gymnosperms differ from angiosperms because gymnosperms
questions.OptionA: produce conspicuous nectar-producing flowers pollinated by insects
questions.OptionB: lack vascular conducting tissues (xylem and phloem)

questions.Subject: Biology
questions.Question: A key difference between monocotyledonous and dicotyledonous flowering plants is that monocots have
questions.OptionA: reticulate leaf venation, vascular bundles in a ring, and a taproot system

questions.Subject: Biology

questions.Subject: Biology

questions.Explanation: Autotrophs (e.g. green plants, photosynthetic bacteria) synthesize complex organic compounds (like glucose) from inorganic CO2 and water using light or chemical energy.

questions.Subject: Biology
questions.Question: The light-dependent stage of photosynthesis takes place in which part of the chloroplast?
questions.Explanation: The light reaction occurs in thylakoid membranes where chlorophyll pigments, photosystems I and II, and ATP synthase complexes are embedded.

questions.Subject: Biology
questions.Question: During the photolysis of water in photosynthesis, water molecules are split into

questions.OptionC: pyruvic acid and lactic acid molecules
questions.OptionD: hydrogen ions (protons), electrons, and oxygen gas

questions.Option_c: pyruvic acid and lactic acid molecules
questions.Option_d: hydrogen ions (protons), electrons, and oxygen gas
questions.Explanation: Photolysis of water (2H2O → 4H+ + 4e- + O2) is driven by light energy in Photosystem II, liberating oxygen gas as a byproduct.

questions.Subject: Biology
questions.Question: The dark stage (light-independent reaction or Calvin cycle) of photosynthesis occurs in the
questions.Explanation: The Calvin cycle takes place in the fluid stroma where the enzyme RuBisCO fixes atmospheric CO2 into carbohydrate precursors.

questions.Subject: Biology
questions.Question: Which of the following is a non-green parasitic plant that absorbs nutrients from host plants via specialized haustoria?
questions.Explanation: Cuscuta (dodder) is a total (holoparasitic) twining plant lacking chlorophyll that penetrates host vascular tissues using sucker-like haustoria.

questions.Subject: Biology
questions.Question: Carnivorous (insectivorous) plants such as Nepenthes and Drosera capture and digest insects primarily to obtain
questions.OptionA: water during severe seasonal drought periods
questions.OptionB: carbon dioxide for photosynthetic sugar production
questions.OptionC: nitrogenous compounds for protein synthesis in nitrogen-deficient soils
questions.Option_a: water during severe seasonal drought periods
questions.Option_b: carbon dioxide for photosynthetic sugar production
questions.Option_c: nitrogenous compounds for protein synthesis in nitrogen-deficient soils
questions.Explanation: Insectivorous plants grow in acidic, nitrogen-poor bogs; they trap and digest insects using proteolytic enzymes to obtain vital nitrates.

questions.Subject: Biology

questions.OptionA: To soften the leaf and break open rigid cell walls
questions.OptionB: To convert insoluble starch into soluble glucose
questions.OptionC: To kill the living protoplasm and stop enzyme activity

questions.Explanation: Boiling in ethanol removes green chlorophyll so that the subsequent blue-black color reaction with iodine solution can be clearly seen.

questions.Subject: Biology
questions.Question: Why must ethanol be heated in a water bath rather than over an open Bunsen burner flame during the starch test?
questions.OptionA: Ethanol is highly flammable and its vapour can easily catch fire

questions.Subject: Biology
questions.Question: Which of the following mineral elements is an essential constituent of the chlorophyll molecule in green plants?
questions.Explanation: A central magnesium (Mg2+) ion is held in the porphyrin ring of chlorophyll; magnesium deficiency causes chlorosis (yellowing of foliage).

questions.Subject: Biology
questions.Question: Holozoic nutrition is characteristic of most animals and involves which sequential steps?
questions.Explanation: Holozoic nutrition proceeds by ingesting solid organic food, digesting it chemically, absorbing simple molecules, assimilating them into tissues, and eliminating undigested wastes.

questions.Subject: Biology
questions.Question: Saprophytic nutrition is exhibited by which of the following organisms?
questions.Explanation: Fungi like Rhizopus and Agaricus are saprophytes that secrete extracellular enzymes onto dead organic matter and absorb the liquefied nutrients.

questions.Subject: Biology
questions.Question: Symbiotic nitrogen-fixing bacteria found in root nodules of leguminous plants belong to the genus
questions.Explanation: Rhizobium species form mutualistic symbiotic associations in root nodules of legumes, fixing inert atmospheric nitrogen into ammonia.

questions.Subject: Biology
questions.Question: Which chemical reagent is used to confirm the presence of starch in a destarched green leaf exposed to sunlight?
questions.Explanation: Iodine solution turns from brownish-yellow to blue-black in the presence of starch.

questions.Subject: Biology
questions.Question: To destarch a potted plant before conducting a photosynthesis experiment, the plant should be kept
questions.OptionA: under continuous bright fluorescent light for three days
questions.OptionB: in a refrigerator at sub-zero temperatures for one hour
questions.OptionC: in a dark cupboard for 24 to 48 hours
questions.OptionD: in a bell jar containing pure oxygen gas for six hours

questions.Subject: Biology
questions.Question: Which of the following environmental factors does NOT act as a limiting factor for photosynthesis in terrestrial green plants?
questions.Explanation: Photosynthesis requires CO2, H2O, light, and appropriate temperature; atmospheric N2 gas cannot be utilized directly and is not a limiting factor for photosynthesis.

questions.Subject: Biology

questions.Option_d: secrete thick waxes that completely repel liquid water
questions.Explanation: Submerged hydrophytes possess thin, dissected leaves with minimal cuticles, absorbing dissolved gases and nutrients directly through epidermal cells.

questions.Subject: Biology
questions.Question: In an experiment demonstrating that oxygen is released during photosynthesis, which aquatic plant is commonly placed under an inverted glass funnel?
questions.Explanation: Elodea or Hydrilla stems are submerged in water under a funnel; glowing splints inserted into the collected gas rekindle, confirming oxygen evolution.

questions.Subject: Biology

questions.Explanation: Enzymes are globular protein catalysts that lower activation energy, accelerate specific cellular reactions, and remain chemically unaltered after the reaction.

questions.Subject: Biology
questions.Question: Which of the following enzymes initiates the chemical digestion of cooked starch in the human mouth?
questions.Explanation: Ptyalin (salivary amylase) is secreted by salivary glands and hydrolyzes cooked starch into the disaccharide maltose in a neutral to slightly alkaline pH.

questions.Subject: Biology
questions.Question: In the human stomach, which acid provides the optimal acidic pH required for the activation of pepsinogen into pepsin?
questions.Explanation: Parietal (oxyntic) cells secrete HCl (pH 1.5–2.0), which destroys ingested microbes and activates inactive pepsinogen into active protease pepsin.

questions.Subject: Biology
questions.Question: The wave-like muscular contractions of the circular and longitudinal muscles that propel food along the alimentary canal are called
questions.Explanation: Peristalsis is the rhythmic, involuntary wave of muscular contraction and relaxation that moves the bolus or chyme along the digestive tract.

questions.Subject: Biology
questions.Question: Bile is synthesized by the liver and stored in the gall bladder. Its primary digestive function is to

questions.OptionB: convert sucrose into glucose and fructose monosaccharides
questions.OptionC: emulsify large fat globules into minute droplets to increase surface area for lipase action
questions.OptionD: destroy beneficial gut microbiota in the ileum
questions.Option_a: hydrolyze peptide bonds in animal proteins into dipeptides
questions.Option_b: convert sucrose into glucose and fructose monosaccharides
questions.Option_c: emulsify large fat globules into minute droplets to increase surface area for lipase action
questions.Option_d: destroy beneficial gut microbiota in the ileum
questions.Explanation: Bile salts (sodium glycocholate and taurocholate) lower surface tension and emulsify lipids, providing an alkaline medium and large surface area for lipases.

questions.Subject: Biology
questions.Question: Which of the following digestive enzymes hydrolyzes proteins into peptides in the duodenum at an alkaline pH?
questions.Explanation: Trypsin is secreted as inactive trypsinogen by the pancreas and acts in the alkaline duodenum (pH ~8.0) to break down proteins and polypeptides.

questions.Subject: Biology

questions.Subject: Biology
questions.Question: Extreme high temperatures (above 60°C) permanently inactivate enzymes because heat
questions.OptionA: converts protein chains into insoluble nucleic acid crystals

questions.Subject: Biology
questions.Question: Which part of the mammalian alimentary canal is specially adapted with villi and microvilli for the absorption of digested nutrients?
questions.Explanation: The ileum has folded walls lined with millions of finger-like villi and microvilli, expanding the internal surface area for nutrient absorption.

questions.Subject: Biology
questions.Question: In the villus of the small intestine, fatty acids and glycerol are absorbed primarily into the central lymphatic vessel called the
questions.Explanation: Digested fats reassemble into chylomicrons and enter the central lacteal vessel of the villus, traveling via the lymphatic system into the bloodstream.

questions.Subject: Biology
questions.Question: Which blood vessel transports water-soluble digested nutrients (glucose, amino acids, minerals) directly from the small intestine to the liver?
questions.Explanation: The hepatic portal vein carries nutrient-rich venous blood from the gastrointestinal capillaries to the liver for metabolic processing and detox.

questions.Subject: Biology
questions.Question: In ruminant mammals (such as cows and sheep), the complex stomach consists of four chambers named
questions.Explanation: Ruminants have a specialized quadricameral stomach: rumen (paunch), reticulum (honeycomb), omasum (manyplies), and abomasum (true glandular stomach).

questions.Subject: Biology
questions.Question: Symbiotic microorganisms (bacteria and ciliated protozoa) in the rumen of herbivores produce which enzyme to digest plant cell walls?
questions.Explanation: Mammals lack endogenous genes for cellulase; symbiotic microbes in the rumen ferment cellulose and hemicellulose into volatile fatty acids.

questions.Subject: Biology

questions.OptionA: mechanically grind ingested grains with the help of swallowed grit and small stones
questions.OptionB: store swallowed food temporarily before digestion
questions.OptionC: secrete concentrated hydrochloric acid and pepsinogen
questions.OptionD: absorb large volumes of water and mineral electrolytes

questions.Subject: Biology
questions.Question: Which of the following test reagents produces a brick-red precipitate when heated with a reducing sugar like glucose?
questions.Explanation: Benedict's reagent contains copper(II) ions which are reduced to insoluble brick-red copper(I) oxide (Cu2O) when heated with reducing sugars.

questions.Subject: Biology
questions.Question: The Biuret test for proteins is positive when the addition of dilute sodium hydroxide and copper(II) sulphate produces a distinct
questions.Explanation: The Biuret reaction detects peptide bonds: cupric ions form a characteristic purple/violet coordination complex in an alkaline medium.

questions.Subject: Biology
questions.Question: The first stage of cellular respiration, known as glycolysis, occurs in the
questions.Explanation: Glycolysis takes place in the cytoplasm and breaks down one glucose molecule into two pyruvate molecules anaerobically, generating a net 2 ATP.

questions.Subject: Biology
questions.Question: The Krebs cycle (citric acid cycle) takes place in which specific cellular compartment?
questions.Explanation: The mitochondrial matrix contains the soluble enzymes responsible for decarboxylating and oxidizing acetyl-CoA during the Krebs cycle.

questions.Subject: Biology

questions.Subject: Biology
