questions.OptionA: gill arches and protected by an operculum
questions.Option_a: gill arches and protected by an operculum
questions.Explanation: Fish gills are mounted on bony gill arches, protected by the operculum, with comb-like gill rakers preventing food debris from damaging delicate filaments.

questions.Subject: Biology
questions.Question: The counter-current flow mechanism in fish gills enhances respiratory efficiency because
questions.OptionA: water and blood flow in the same direction, reaching quick osmotic equilibrium
questions.OptionB: blood flows across the gill lamellae in the opposite direction to water flow, maintaining a continuous oxygen diffusion gradient
questions.OptionC: it prevents carbon dioxide from dissolving into the surrounding aquatic medium
questions.OptionD: it allows the fish to breathe atmospheric nitrogen gas during low tides
questions.Option_a: water and blood flow in the same direction, reaching quick osmotic equilibrium
questions.Option_b: blood flows across the gill lamellae in the opposite direction to water flow, maintaining a continuous oxygen diffusion gradient
questions.Option_c: it prevents carbon dioxide from dissolving into the surrounding aquatic medium
questions.Option_d: it allows the fish to breathe atmospheric nitrogen gas during low tides
questions.Explanation: Counter-current exchange ensures blood meets water of progressively higher oxygen concentration, maximizing oxygen extraction up to 80-85%.

questions.Subject: Biology
questions.Question: In mammals, the actual sites of gaseous exchange in the lungs are microscopic air sacs called
questions.Explanation: The lungs contain hundreds of millions of thin-walled alveoli surrounded by capillary plexuses where O2 diffuses into blood and CO2 diffuses out.

questions.Subject: Biology
questions.Question: During inhalation (inspiration) in humans, what changes occur in the diaphragm and external intercostal muscles?
questions.OptionA: Diaphragm relaxes and domes upward; external intercostals relax, lowering the ribs
questions.OptionB: Diaphragm and ribs remain completely stationary while lungs expand mechanically
questions.OptionC: Diaphragm pushes upward while thoracic cavity volume decreases significantly
questions.OptionD: Diaphragm contracts and flattens; external intercostal muscles contract, lifting the rib cage up and out
questions.Option_a: Diaphragm relaxes and domes upward; external intercostals relax, lowering the ribs
questions.Option_b: Diaphragm and ribs remain completely stationary while lungs expand mechanically
questions.Option_c: Diaphragm pushes upward while thoracic cavity volume decreases significantly
questions.Option_d: Diaphragm contracts and flattens; external intercostal muscles contract, lifting the rib cage up and out
questions.Explanation: Inhalation is active: diaphragm contraction flattens it, intercostals raise the ribs, increasing thoracic volume and decreasing pulmonary pressure below atmospheric.

questions.Subject: Biology
questions.Question: In woody stems of dicotyledonous plants, gaseous exchange between internal living tissues and atmosphere occurs through
questions.Explanation: Lenticels are loose, porous spongy openings in the impermeable corky periderm (bark) of woody stems and roots that permit gas exchange.

questions.Subject: Biology
questions.Question: The stomata of green leaves typically open during the day and close at night because
questions.OptionA: guard cells lose all cytoplasmic organelles in the presence of sunlight
questions.OptionB: guard cells take in water and become turgid in light, causing the stomatal pore to curve open
questions.OptionC: epidermal cells shrink drastically when carbon dioxide is consumed
questions.OptionD: cuticle layers dissolve in daytime heat and solidify at night
questions.Option_a: guard cells lose all cytoplasmic organelles in the presence of sunlight
questions.Option_b: guard cells take in water and become turgid in light, causing the stomatal pore to curve open
questions.Option_c: epidermal cells shrink drastically when carbon dioxide is consumed
questions.Option_d: cuticle layers dissolve in daytime heat and solidify at night
questions.Explanation: Daytime photosynthesis increases solutes (K+ and sugars) in guard cells; water enters by osmosis, turgor pressure rises, and the thick inner wall bows open.

questions.Subject: Biology
questions.Question: What chemical substance is commonly placed inside a respirometer to absorb carbon dioxide gas when measuring oxygen uptake of germinating seeds?
questions.Explanation: KOH or NaOH pellets absorb exhaled CO2, so the volume change in the manometer manometer reflects solely the oxygen consumed by respiration.

questions.Subject: Biology
questions.Question: The respiratory quotient (RQ) is calculated as the ratio of
questions.OptionA: Volume of O2 consumed to Volume of CO2 evolved
questions.OptionB: Total ATP produced to Total glucose consumed
questions.OptionC: Volume of water transpired to Volume of water absorbed
questions.OptionD: Volume of CO2 evolved to Volume of O2 consumed
questions.Option_a: Volume of O2 consumed to Volume of CO2 evolved
questions.Option_b: Total ATP produced to Total glucose consumed
questions.Option_c: Volume of water transpired to Volume of water absorbed
questions.Option_d: Volume of CO2 evolved to Volume of O2 consumed
questions.Explanation: Respiratory Quotient (RQ) = (Volume of CO2 produced) / (Volume of O2 consumed). Carbohydrates have an RQ of 1.0, while fats are ~0.7.

questions.Subject: Biology
questions.Question: The basic functional, structural, and microscopic excretory unit of the mammalian kidney is the
questions.Explanation: Each kidney contains over a million nephrons, each consisting of a glomerulus, Bowman's capsule, proximal tubule, loop of Henle, and distal tubule.

questions.Subject: Biology
questions.Question: Ultrafiltration in the mammalian nephron occurs between the
questions.OptionA: loop of Henle and collecting duct
questions.OptionC: proximal convoluted tubule and renal vein
questions.Option_a: loop of Henle and collecting duct
questions.Option_c: proximal convoluted tubule and renal vein
questions.Explanation: High hydrostatic blood pressure in the afferent arteriole forces water, urea, salts, and glucose across the fenestrated glomerular capillaries into Bowman's capsule.

questions.Subject: Biology
questions.Question: Which of the following blood constituents is normally absent from the glomerular filtrate of a healthy person?
questions.OptionC: Blood plasma proteins (albumin) and red blood cells
questions.Option_c: Blood plasma proteins (albumin) and red blood cells
questions.Explanation: Plasma proteins and blood cells are too large to pass through the glomerular filtration barrier and podocyte slit diaphragms, remaining in blood.

questions.Subject: Biology
questions.Question: In the proximal convoluted tubule (PCT) of the nephron, useful substances such as glucose and amino acids are reabsorbed by
questions.OptionC: osmotic lysis of tubular epithelial cells
questions.Option_c: osmotic lysis of tubular epithelial cells
questions.Explanation: Under normal physiological conditions, 100% of filtered glucose and amino acids are selectively reabsorbed by active transport back into peritubular capillaries.

questions.Subject: Biology
questions.Question: The Loop of Henle is responsible for creating a hypertonic medullary osmotic gradient which enables the kidney to
questions.OptionA: reabsorb water and produce concentrated (hypertonic) urine
questions.OptionB: synthesize urea from carbon dioxide and ammonia
questions.OptionD: secrete digestive enzymes into the renal pelvis
questions.Option_a: reabsorb water and produce concentrated (hypertonic) urine
questions.Option_b: synthesize urea from carbon dioxide and ammonia
questions.Option_d: secrete digestive enzymes into the renal pelvis
questions.Explanation: The counter-current multiplier system in the loop of Henle creates a steep medullary salt gradient, enabling the collecting duct to conserve water.

questions.Subject: Biology
questions.Question: Which hormone secreted by the posterior pituitary gland regulates water reabsorption in the collecting ducts of the kidney?
questions.Explanation: When blood osmotic pressure rises (dehydration), the pituitary releases ADH, which increases collecting duct aquaporin permeability, concentrating urine.

questions.Subject: Biology
questions.Question: What is the primary excretory organ in insects (such as cockroaches and grasshoppers)?
questions.Explanation: Malpighian tubules are slender blind-ended tubules lying in the insect hemolymph that extract potassium urate and precipitate uric acid into the gut.

questions.Subject: Biology
questions.Question: Flatworms (Platyhelminthes like Planaria and tapeworms) eliminate excretory wastes and maintain osmoregulation using
questions.Explanation: Flame cells contain tufts of beating cilia that propel fluid through excretory canals to nephridiopores, maintaining osmotic balance in flatworms.

questions.Subject: Biology
questions.Question: Earthworms (annelids) excrete metabolic wastes through segmented tubular structures called
questions.Explanation: Metanephridia occur in pairs in each earthworm segment; ciliated nephrostomes collect coelomic fluid and excrete nitrogenous waste through nephridiopores.

questions.Subject: Biology
questions.Question: Which of the following represents the main nitrogenous excretory product in birds and terrestrial reptiles?
questions.Explanation: Uric acid is insoluble and non-toxic, requiring minimal water for excretion (uricotelism), which conserves water in arid habitats and inside eggs.

questions.Subject: Biology
questions.Question: Freshwater bony fishes are described as ammonotelic because they primarily excrete
questions.OptionC: ammonia, which is highly soluble in abundant surrounding water
questions.Option_c: ammonia, which is highly soluble in abundant surrounding water
questions.Explanation: Ammonia is extremely toxic but highly water-soluble; freshwater organisms excrete it rapidly through gill surfaces directly into the abundant water.

questions.Subject: Biology
questions.Question: Which of the following is an excretory product eliminated by the human skin through sweat glands?
questions.OptionD: Water, mineral salts (NaCl), and traces of urea
questions.Option_d: Water, mineral salts (NaCl), and traces of urea
questions.Explanation: Sweat glands (eccrine glands) excrete perspiration consisting predominantly of water, sodium chloride, and minor amounts of urea and lactic acid.

questions.Subject: Biology
questions.Question: In Amoeba, osmoregulation is performed by the
questions.Explanation: Living in hypotonic freshwater, water continuously enters Amoeba by endosmosis; the contractile vacuole collects and pumps out excess water.

questions.Subject: Biology
questions.Question: Guttation in herbaceous plants is defined as the
questions.OptionA: loss of water vapour through stomata during sunny afternoons
questions.OptionB: exudation of liquid water droplets from hydathodes at leaf margins under high root pressure and humidity
questions.OptionC: absorptive uptake of soil moisture by root hair cells
questions.OptionD: translocation of manufactured sucrose along phloem sieve plates
questions.Option_a: loss of water vapour through stomata during sunny afternoons
questions.Option_b: exudation of liquid water droplets from hydathodes at leaf margins under high root pressure and humidity
questions.Option_c: absorptive uptake of soil moisture by root hair cells
questions.Option_d: translocation of manufactured sucrose along phloem sieve plates
questions.Explanation: Guttation occurs through specialized marginal pores (hydathodes) when high soil moisture and low nighttime transpiration create excessive hydrostatic root pressure.

questions.Subject: Biology
questions.Question: Which of the following is a plant excretory/metabolic waste product utilized commercially by humans as medicine?
questions.OptionC: Quinine (from the bark of Cinchona tree)
questions.Option_c: Quinine (from the bark of Cinchona tree)
questions.Explanation: Quinine is an alkaloid waste product extracted from the bark of the Cinchona tree, historically used worldwide to treat malaria.

questions.Subject: Biology
questions.Question: The removal of excess amino acids in the mammalian liver by removing the amino group to form urea is known as
questions.Explanation: Deamination strips the toxic -NH2 amino group from excess amino acids, converting it into ammonia and subsequently into urea via the ornithine cycle.

questions.Subject: Biology
questions.Question: What condition results when the islets of Langerhans in the pancreas fail to secrete sufficient insulin, leading to glucose appearing in urine?
questions.Explanation: Diabetes mellitus is characterized by hyperglycemia; excess blood glucose exceeds the renal threshold and spills into urine (glucosuria).

questions.Subject: Biology
questions.Question: Which of the following organisms relies on a hydrostatic skeleton for locomotion and maintaining body form?
questions.Explanation: Soft-bodied invertebrates like earthworms have a fluid-filled coelomic cavity under turgor pressure against which circular and longitudinal muscles act.

questions.Subject: Biology
questions.Question: The exoskeleton of arthropods (such as insects, crabs, and millipedes) is composed primarily of
questions.OptionC: chitin strengthened by proteins and calcium salts
questions.Option_c: chitin strengthened by proteins and calcium salts
questions.Explanation: Arthropod exoskeletons consist of chitin, an insoluble nitrogenous polysaccharide cross-linked with sclerotized proteins and minerals.

questions.Subject: Biology
questions.Question: In the human axial skeleton, which of the following bones forms part of the vertebral column?
questions.Explanation: The axial skeleton comprises the skull, vertebral column (cervical, thoracic, lumbar, sacral, caudal), ribs, and sternum. Clavicle and femur belong to the appendicular skeleton.

questions.Subject: Biology
questions.Question: How many vertebrae make up the cervical (neck) region in typical mammals, including humans and giraffes?
questions.Explanation: Almost all mammals possess exactly 7 cervical vertebrae, ranging from tiny bats to long-necked giraffes.

questions.Subject: Biology
questions.Question: The first cervical vertebra that articulates directly with the occipital condyles of the skull to permit nodding movements is called the
questions.Explanation: The atlas (C1) lacks a centrum and supports the skull, articulating with occipital condyles to allow 'yes' nodding motions.

questions.Subject: Biology
questions.Question: The second cervical vertebra that possesses an odontoid peg (process) around which the head rotates side to side is the
questions.Explanation: The axis (C2) features an odontoid process (dens) serving as a pivot for the atlas, facilitating rotational 'no' head movements.

questions.Subject: Biology
questions.Question: Which of the following bones is the longest, strongest, and heaviest bone in the human body?
questions.Explanation: The femur is the thigh bone of the lower appendicular skeleton, supporting body weight during bipedal standing and locomotion.

questions.Subject: Biology
questions.Question: The pectoral girdle in mammals consists of which pair of bones?
questions.Explanation: The pectoral (shoulder) girdle connects the upper limbs to the axial skeleton and comprises the flat triangular scapula and slender clavicle.

questions.Subject: Biology
questions.Question: The pelvic girdle articulates with the head of the femur at a deep cup-shaped socket known as the
questions.Explanation: The acetabulum is the deep socket formed by the fusion of ilium, ischium, and pubis where the spherical head of the femur articulates.

questions.Subject: Biology
questions.Question: Which type of movable joint permits rotation in all planes and is found at the shoulder and hip?
questions.Explanation: Ball-and-socket joints (glenohumeral and hip joints) allow multiaxial movement: flexion, extension, abduction, adduction, and circumduction.

questions.Subject: Biology
questions.Question: The elbow joint and knee joint are examples of which type of synovial joint?
questions.Explanation: Hinge joints restrict movement to a single plane (uniaxial flexion and extension), resembling the mechanical hinge of a door.

questions.Subject: Biology
questions.Question: In synovial joints, what fluid lubricates the articulating cartilage surfaces to reduce friction during movement?
questions.Explanation: Synovial fluid is secreted by the synovial membrane lining the joint capsule, lubricating cartilage and nourishing chondrocytes.

questions.Subject: Biology
questions.Question: Tough, inelastic bands of dense fibrous connective tissue that attach skeletal muscles to bones are called
questions.Explanation: Tendons connect contractile muscles to rigid bones, transmitting muscular tension to cause movement. Ligaments connect bone to bone.

questions.Subject: Biology
questions.Question: Ligaments in the human skeletal system function primarily to
questions.OptionA: synthesize red blood cells in the marrow cavity
questions.OptionB: secrete hydrochloric acid to remodel bone tissue
questions.OptionC: connect bone to bone and stabilize joints against dislocation
questions.OptionD: contract involuntarily to pump venous blood back to the heart
questions.Option_a: synthesize red blood cells in the marrow cavity
questions.Option_b: secrete hydrochloric acid to remodel bone tissue
questions.Option_c: connect bone to bone and stabilize joints against dislocation
questions.Option_d: contract involuntarily to pump venous blood back to the heart
questions.Explanation: Ligaments are tough, elastic fibrous cords that join articulating bones together across a joint, preventing hyperextension and dislocation.

questions.Subject: Biology
questions.Question: Antagonistic muscle action is exemplified in the human arm when bending the elbow by the
questions.OptionA: contraction of both biceps and triceps muscles simultaneously
questions.OptionB: relaxation of all pectoral and arm muscles
questions.OptionC: contraction of the triceps while the biceps remains inert
questions.OptionD: contraction of the biceps and simultaneous relaxation of the triceps
questions.Option_a: contraction of both biceps and triceps muscles simultaneously
questions.Option_b: relaxation of all pectoral and arm muscles
questions.Option_c: contraction of the triceps while the biceps remains inert
questions.Option_d: contraction of the biceps and simultaneous relaxation of the triceps
questions.Explanation: Antagonistic muscles operate in opposing pairs: flexing the forearm requires contraction of the biceps (flexor) and reciprocal relaxation of the triceps (extensor).

questions.Subject: Biology
questions.Question: Ecdysis (moulting) is biologically necessary in arthropods because the
questions.OptionA: rigid chitinous exoskeleton does not expand, restricting further organismal growth
questions.OptionC: organism must shed internal bones to reduce weight for flight
questions.OptionD: arthropod must change its gender every season
questions.Option_a: rigid chitinous exoskeleton does not expand, restricting further organismal growth
questions.Option_c: organism must shed internal bones to reduce weight for flight
questions.Option_d: arthropod must change its gender every season
questions.Explanation: The hard cuticular exoskeleton cannot stretch; arthropods must periodically shed their old cuticle and expand a new soft cuticle beneath before it hardens.

questions.Subject: Biology
questions.Question: Which of the following nutritional deficiencies leads to soft, weak, and deformed bones (rickets in children and osteomalacia in adults)?
questions.OptionB: Deficiency of Vitamin D and Calcium
questions.Option_b: Deficiency of Vitamin D and Calcium
questions.Explanation: Vitamin D is essential for intestinal calcium absorption; deficiency causes defective mineralization of osteoid matrix, producing rickets.

questions.Subject: Biology
questions.Question: In higher plants, water and dissolved mineral salts are transported from the roots up to the leaves through the
questions.OptionA: phloem sieve tubes and companion cells
questions.Option_a: phloem sieve tubes and companion cells
questions.Explanation: Xylem is the vascular tissue responsible for unidirectional transport of water and inorganic ions (transpiration stream) from roots to aerial parts.

questions.Subject: Biology
questions.Question: The primary physiological mechanism driving the upward ascent of sap in tall trees is the
questions.OptionA: hydrostatic pressure generated by the phloem companion cells
questions.OptionB: gravitational pull acting on stem cortex cells
questions.OptionC: osmotic attraction of chlorophyll pigments for mineral salts
questions.OptionD: transpiration pull created by water evaporation from leaves
questions.Option_a: hydrostatic pressure generated by the phloem companion cells
questions.Option_b: gravitational pull acting on stem cortex cells
questions.Option_c: osmotic attraction of chlorophyll pigments for mineral salts
questions.Option_d: transpiration pull created by water evaporation from leaves
questions.Explanation: Evaporation of water through stomata sets up negative hydrostatic pressure (suction tension) in leaf mesophyll that pulls water columns up xylem vessels.

questions.Subject: Biology
questions.Question: The cohesion-tension theory explains that water columns remain unbroken in xylem vessels due to the
questions.OptionA: strong hydrogen bonds (cohesion) between water molecules and adhesion to xylem walls
questions.OptionB: active contraction of smooth muscles in the stem pericycle
questions.OptionC: rapid binary division of cambium cells
questions.OptionD: secretion of waxy suberin along the vascular bundle
questions.Option_a: strong hydrogen bonds (cohesion) between water molecules and adhesion to xylem walls
questions.Option_b: active contraction of smooth muscles in the stem pericycle
questions.Option_c: rapid binary division of cambium cells
questions.Option_d: secretion of waxy suberin along the vascular bundle
questions.Explanation: Cohesion (intermolecular attraction between water molecules) and adhesion (attraction to lignified hydrophilic xylem walls) maintain continuous sap columns under tension.

questions.Subject: Biology
questions.Question: Transpiration is biologically defined as the
questions.OptionA: exudation of mineral liquid from hydathode leaf margins
questions.OptionB: loss of water in the form of water vapour from the aerial parts of a plant, primarily through stomata
questions.OptionC: transport of manufactured sucrose from leaves to storage roots
questions.OptionD: intake of liquid water by root hairs across the soil gradient
questions.Option_a: exudation of mineral liquid from hydathode leaf margins
questions.Option_b: loss of water in the form of water vapour from the aerial parts of a plant, primarily through stomata
questions.Option_c: transport of manufactured sucrose from leaves to storage roots
questions.Option_d: intake of liquid water by root hairs across the soil gradient
questions.Explanation: Transpiration is the evaporative loss of water vapor from plant surfaces, with over 90% occurring through stomatal pores in foliage leaves.

questions.Subject: Biology
questions.Question: Which instrument is used in plant physiology laboratories to measure the rate of water uptake (transpiration rate) by a leafy shoot?
questions.Explanation: A potometer (e.g. Ganong's potometer) measures the rate of water absorption by a severed leafy shoot, which closely approximates the transpiration rate.

questions.Subject: Biology
questions.Question: Which of the following environmental conditions will significantly increase the rate of transpiration in plants?
questions.OptionA: Cool ambient temperature, complete darkness, and 100% relative humidity
questions.OptionB: Submerging the entire plant in liquid mineral oil
questions.OptionC: Covering both upper and lower leaf surfaces with petroleum jelly
questions.OptionD: High ambient temperature, bright sunlight, low relative humidity, and windy conditions
questions.Option_a: Cool ambient temperature, complete darkness, and 100% relative humidity
questions.Option_b: Submerging the entire plant in liquid mineral oil
questions.Option_c: Covering both upper and lower leaf surfaces with petroleum jelly
questions.Option_d: High ambient temperature, bright sunlight, low relative humidity, and windy conditions
questions.Explanation: Warmth, bright light (opening stomata), dry air (steep vapor gradient), and air currents (sweeping away boundary moisture layers) accelerate transpiration.

questions.Subject: Biology
questions.Question: The translocation of manufactured food substances (such as sucrose) from leaves to storage organs occurs via the
questions.Explanation: Phloem tissue translocates organic nutrients (principally sucrose and amino acids) bidirectionally from source tissues (leaves) to sink tissues (roots, fruits).

questions.Subject: Biology
questions.Question: In a classic ringing (girdling) experiment on a woody stem, a complete ring of bark including the phloem is removed. What is the immediate effect?
questions.OptionA: Water transport to the upper leaves ceases immediately, causing wilting within minutes
questions.OptionB: Sugar accumulates above the ring causing swelling, while roots are eventually starved of organic nutrients
questions.OptionC: The plant instantly sheds all its floral petals
questions.OptionD: New xylem vessels spontaneously emerge from the exposed cortex
questions.Option_a: Water transport to the upper leaves ceases immediately, causing wilting within minutes
questions.Option_b: Sugar accumulates above the ring causing swelling, while roots are eventually starved of organic nutrients
questions.Option_c: The plant instantly sheds all its floral petals
questions.Option_d: New xylem vessels spontaneously emerge from the exposed cortex
questions.Explanation: Ringing removes the phloem but leaves the xylem intact; upward water flow continues, but downward sugar flow is blocked, forming a swollen callus above the cut.

questions.Subject: Biology
questions.Question: Which specialized plant cells possess sieve plates and lack a nucleus at functional maturity, relying on companion cells for metabolic support?
questions.Explanation: Mature sieve tube members possess perforated end walls (sieve plates) and peripheral cytoplasm devoid of nuclei, sustained by adjacent nucleated companion cells.

questions.Subject: Biology
questions.Question: Water enters the root hair cell from the surrounding soil solution by the process of
questions.OptionC: hydrostatic filtration under arterial blood pressure
questions.OptionD: osmosis across the selectively permeable plasma membrane
questions.Option_c: hydrostatic filtration under arterial blood pressure
questions.Option_d: osmosis across the selectively permeable plasma membrane
questions.Explanation: Soil water typically has a higher water potential than the hypertonic cell sap of root hairs; water moves down the potential gradient via osmosis.

questions.Subject: Biology
questions.Question: In the plant root, the Casparian strip of the endodermis forces water and minerals to cross via the symplast pathway because the strip is impregnated with
questions.OptionA: suberin and lignin, which are completely impermeable to water
questions.OptionC: pectin that expands in alkaline solutions
questions.OptionD: calcium carbonate shells that attract light
questions.Option_a: suberin and lignin, which are completely impermeable to water
questions.Option_c: pectin that expands in alkaline solutions
questions.Option_d: calcium carbonate shells that attract light
questions.Explanation: The Casparian strip is a hydrophobic suberized band in radial endodermal walls that blocks the apoplastic route, forcing water through living protoplasts.

questions.Subject: Biology
questions.Question: Which morphological adaptation helps xerophytic plants (such as cacti and marram grass) reduce water loss by transpiration?
questions.OptionA: Broad, thin foliage leaves with numerous exposed stomata
questions.OptionB: Thick waxy cuticles, sunken stomata, and reduction of leaves into spines
questions.OptionC: Absence of root systems and possession of large aerenchyma spaces
questions.OptionD: Keeping stomata continuously open during scorching midday hours
questions.Option_a: Broad, thin foliage leaves with numerous exposed stomata
questions.Option_b: Thick waxy cuticles, sunken stomata, and reduction of leaves into spines
questions.Option_c: Absence of root systems and possession of large aerenchyma spaces
questions.Option_d: Keeping stomata continuously open during scorching midday hours
questions.Explanation: Xerophytes minimize transpiration through succulent water-storing tissues, thick cuticles, sunken stomatal pits, and leaves modified into protective spines.

questions.Subject: Biology
questions.Question: Root pressure in plants is generated primarily by the
questions.OptionA: rapid evaporation of water from foliage leaf veins
questions.OptionB: mechanical contraction of the root cap
questions.OptionC: active accumulation of mineral ions in the root xylem, lowering water potential and drawing in water osmotically
questions.OptionD: downward translocation of starch granules from flowers
questions.Option_a: rapid evaporation of water from foliage leaf veins
questions.Option_b: mechanical contraction of the root cap
questions.Option_c: active accumulation of mineral ions in the root xylem, lowering water potential and drawing in water osmotically
questions.Option_d: downward translocation of starch granules from flowers
questions.Explanation: Active transport of mineral ions into the root stele creates an osmotic gradient that drives water into the xylem, generating positive root pressure.

questions.Subject: Biology
questions.Question: The pressure-flow (mass-flow) hypothesis of phloem translocation proposed by Ernst Münch relies on
questions.OptionA: capillary action through narrow lignified annular rings
questions.OptionB: direct pumping by muscular contractions of companion cells
questions.OptionC: continuous gravitational settling of dense starch grains
questions.OptionD: turgor pressure gradients generated by osmotic water uptake at sources and solute unloading at sinks
questions.Option_a: capillary action through narrow lignified annular rings
questions.Option_b: direct pumping by muscular contractions of companion cells
questions.Option_c: continuous gravitational settling of dense starch grains
questions.Option_d: turgor pressure gradients generated by osmotic water uptake at sources and solute unloading at sinks
questions.Explanation: Active sucrose loading at sources lowers water potential, drawing water and raising turgor pressure; at sinks, unloading drops turgor, driving bulk mass flow.

questions.Subject: Biology
questions.Question: Wilting in herbaceous plants occurs when the rate of
questions.OptionA: transpiration exceeds the rate of water absorption by roots, causing cells to lose turgor
questions.OptionB: water absorption exceeds the rate of stomatal evaporation
questions.OptionC: photosynthesis is higher than the rate of respiration
questions.OptionD: phloem translocation increases tenfold in bright sunlight
questions.Option_a: transpiration exceeds the rate of water absorption by roots, causing cells to lose turgor
questions.Option_b: water absorption exceeds the rate of stomatal evaporation
questions.Option_c: photosynthesis is higher than the rate of respiration
questions.Option_d: phloem translocation increases tenfold in bright sunlight
questions.Explanation: When transpiration outpaces root water uptake, leaf and stem parenchyma cells lose water, turgidity drops, and the shoot wilts and droops flaccidly.

questions.Subject: Biology
questions.Question: Turgor pressure in plant cells is vital because it
questions.OptionA: destroys pathogenic fungal spores in the intercellular spaces
questions.OptionB: provides mechanical support and rigidity to herbaceous non-woody tissues
questions.OptionC: converts glucose molecules into carbon dioxide and water
questions.OptionD: prevents water from entering root hair membranes
questions.Option_a: destroys pathogenic fungal spores in the intercellular spaces
questions.Option_b: provides mechanical support and rigidity to herbaceous non-woody tissues
questions.Option_c: converts glucose molecules into carbon dioxide and water
questions.Option_d: prevents water from entering root hair membranes
questions.Explanation: Turgor pressure pushes the plasma membrane firmly against the cell wall, keeping young stems, leaves, and petals erect and structurally supported.

questions.Subject: Biology
questions.Question: Which of the following is an adaptation of hydrophytes (aquatic plants like water lily)?
questions.OptionA: Sunken stomata surrounded by dense epidermal hairs
questions.OptionB: A thick, heavily suberized woody periderm on leaves
questions.OptionC: Extensive aerenchyma tissue for buoyancy and stomata restricted to the upper leaf surface
questions.OptionD: Deep taproots extending ten meters into the river bed
questions.Option_a: Sunken stomata surrounded by dense epidermal hairs
questions.Option_b: A thick, heavily suberized woody periderm on leaves
questions.Option_c: Extensive aerenchyma tissue for buoyancy and stomata restricted to the upper leaf surface
questions.Option_d: Deep taproots extending ten meters into the river bed
questions.Explanation: Floating hydrophytes feature air-filled aerenchyma for floatation and gas exchange, with stomata confined to the upper sun-exposed lamina surface.

questions.Subject: Biology
questions.Question: An open circulatory system is characteristic of which of the following animals?
questions.Explanation: In insects and other arthropods, blood (hemolymph) is pumped by a tubular dorsal heart into open body cavities (hemocoel), bathing tissues directly.

questions.Subject: Biology
questions.Question: In a closed circulatory system, blood flows continuously within
questions.OptionA: a closed network of blood vessels (arteries, capillaries, and veins)
questions.OptionB: open coelomic body sinuses without endothelial linings
questions.OptionC: the digestive tract alongside ingested dietary chyme
questions.OptionD: the lymphatic ducts without entering capillaries
questions.Option_a: a closed network of blood vessels (arteries, capillaries, and veins)
questions.Option_b: open coelomic body sinuses without endothelial linings
questions.Option_c: the digestive tract alongside ingested dietary chyme
questions.Option_d: the lymphatic ducts without entering capillaries
questions.Explanation: Closed circulation confines blood entirely inside distinct blood vessels, allowing higher hydrostatic pressure and rapid, targeted transport.

questions.Subject: Biology
questions.Question: In mammals, the heart is described as having a double circulation because
questions.OptionA: the heart possesses two identical right and left pacemakers
questions.OptionB: blood passes through the heart twice during one complete circuit of the body (pulmonary and systemic circuits)
questions.OptionC: oxygenated and deoxygenated blood mix freely in the single ventricle
questions.OptionD: blood flows simultaneously forward and backward through the aorta
questions.Option_a: the heart possesses two identical right and left pacemakers
questions.Option_b: blood passes through the heart twice during one complete circuit of the body (pulmonary and systemic circuits)
questions.Option_c: oxygenated and deoxygenated blood mix freely in the single ventricle
questions.Option_d: blood flows simultaneously forward and backward through the aorta
questions.Explanation: Double circulation comprises the pulmonary circuit (heart → lungs → heart) and the systemic circuit (heart → body tissues → heart).

questions.Subject: Biology
questions.Question: Which chamber of the mammalian heart has the thickest muscular wall (myocardium)?
questions.Explanation: The left ventricle pumps oxygenated blood against high systemic vascular resistance across the entire body via the aorta, requiring the thickest muscular wall.

questions.Subject: Biology
questions.Question: The bicuspid (mitral) valve is located between the
questions.Explanation: The bicuspid (mitral) valve guards the left atrioventricular orifice, preventing the backflow of oxygenated blood into the left atrium during ventricular systole.

questions.Subject: Biology
questions.Question: Arteries differ structurally from veins because arteries have
questions.OptionA: thick, elastic muscular walls, narrow lumens, and no valves (except at exits of the heart)
questions.OptionB: thin walls, wide lumens, and numerous pocket valves along their length
questions.OptionC: walls consisting only of a single layer of squamous endothelial cells
questions.OptionD: valves that continuously pump deoxygenated blood backward
questions.Option_a: thick, elastic muscular walls, narrow lumens, and no valves (except at exits of the heart)
questions.Option_b: thin walls, wide lumens, and numerous pocket valves along their length
questions.Option_c: walls consisting only of a single layer of squamous endothelial cells
questions.Option_d: valves that continuously pump deoxygenated blood backward
questions.Explanation: Arteries carry blood under high pulsating pressure from the heart and feature thick tunica media with elastic fibers, narrow lumens, and lack valves.

questions.Subject: Biology
questions.Question: Which blood vessel carries oxygenated blood from the lungs back to the left atrium of the mammalian heart?
questions.Explanation: Unlike all other veins which carry deoxygenated blood, pulmonary veins transport freshly oxygenated blood from alveolar lung capillaries to the heart.

questions.Subject: Biology
questions.Question: The natural pacemaker of the mammalian heart that initiates electrical cardiac impulses is the
questions.Explanation: The SA node, situated in the right atrial wall, generates spontaneous rhythmic action potentials that dictate heart rate, acting as the primary pacemaker.

questions.Subject: Biology
questions.Question: Which of the following blood cellular components is enucleated and biconcave, packed with hemoglobin for oxygen transport?
questions.Explanation: Mammalian erythrocytes lack nuclei, mitochondria, and ribosomes, maximizing internal volume for hemoglobin and ensuring flexible transit through capillaries.

questions.Subject: Biology
questions.Question: Which type of white blood cell produces specific antibodies to neutralize foreign pathogens and toxins?
questions.Explanation: B-lymphocytes differentiate into plasma cells that synthesize and secrete antigen-specific immunoglobulins (antibodies) as part of humoral immunity.

questions.Subject: Biology
questions.Question: Blood platelets (thrombocytes) play a critical role in
questions.OptionA: carrying dissolved glucose molecules across intestinal villi
questions.OptionB: initiating blood clotting and preventing excessive hemorrhage following injury
questions.OptionC: secreting hydrochloric acid into the blood plasma
questions.OptionD: engulfing bacterial invaders via active phagocytosis
questions.Option_a: carrying dissolved glucose molecules across intestinal villi
questions.Option_b: initiating blood clotting and preventing excessive hemorrhage following injury
questions.Option_c: secreting hydrochloric acid into the blood plasma
questions.Option_d: engulfing bacterial invaders via active phagocytosis
questions.Explanation: Platelets adhere to damaged vascular endothelium and release thromboplastin, initiating the enzymatic cascade that converts prothrombin to thrombin.

questions.Subject: Biology
questions.Question: In the chemical cascade of blood clotting, the conversion of soluble fibrinogen into insoluble fibrin threads is catalyzed by the enzyme
questions.OptionC: thrombin (in the presence of calcium ions)
questions.Option_c: thrombin (in the presence of calcium ions)
questions.Explanation: Thrombin cleaves fibrinogen into insoluble fibrin monomers that polymerize to form a mesh trapping red blood cells and creating a stable hemostatic clot.

questions.Subject: Biology
questions.Question: An individual possessing blood group O is called a universal donor because their red blood cells
questions.OptionA: contain both A and B antibodies inside their nucleus
questions.OptionC: can synthesize hemoglobin in donor plasma without oxygen
questions.OptionD: lack both A and B antigens on their surface, preventing agglutination in recipients
questions.Option_a: contain both A and B antibodies inside their nucleus
questions.Option_c: can synthesize hemoglobin in donor plasma without oxygen
questions.Option_d: lack both A and B antigens on their surface, preventing agglutination in recipients
questions.Explanation: Group O erythrocytes display neither antigen A nor antigen B; therefore, they do not trigger immune agglutination when transfused into recipients.

questions.Subject: Biology
questions.Question: Agglutination occurs during an incompatible blood transfusion because
questions.OptionA: antibodies in the recipient's plasma react with and clump antigens on the donor's red blood cells
questions.OptionB: blood plasma boils due to elevated metabolic temperature
questions.OptionC: platelets consume all red blood cells by phagocytosis
questions.OptionD: blood vessels immediately dissolve their smooth muscular walls
questions.Option_a: antibodies in the recipient's plasma react with and clump antigens on the donor's red blood cells
questions.Option_b: blood plasma boils due to elevated metabolic temperature
questions.Option_c: platelets consume all red blood cells by phagocytosis
questions.Option_d: blood vessels immediately dissolve their smooth muscular walls
questions.Explanation: If donor red blood cells carry foreign antigens, the recipient's matching plasma antibodies bind and cross-link them, causing lethal clumping (agglutination).

questions.Subject: Biology
questions.Question: The lymphatic system is an auxiliary vascular network that functions to
questions.OptionA: pump oxygenated blood directly from the kidneys to the brain
questions.OptionB: drain excess tissue fluid back into the venous bloodstream and defend against infection via lymph nodes
questions.OptionD: synthesize bile salts from damaged erythrocytes
questions.Option_a: pump oxygenated blood directly from the kidneys to the brain
questions.Option_b: drain excess tissue fluid back into the venous bloodstream and defend against infection via lymph nodes
questions.Option_d: synthesize bile salts from damaged erythrocytes
questions.Explanation: Lymphatic capillaries collect interstitial fluid (lymph) that escapes blood capillaries, filter pathogens through lymph nodes, and return fluid to subclavian veins.

questions.Subject: Biology
questions.Question: Erythroblastosis fetalis (hemolytic disease of the newborn) can occur when an
questions.OptionA: Rh-positive mother carries an Rh-negative fetus
questions.OptionB: O-group father marries an AB-group mother
questions.OptionC: Rh-negative mother carries an Rh-positive fetus during a second or subsequent pregnancy
questions.OptionD: expectant mother lacks dietary calcium salts
questions.Option_a: Rh-positive mother carries an Rh-negative fetus
questions.Option_b: O-group father marries an AB-group mother
questions.Option_c: Rh-negative mother carries an Rh-positive fetus during a second or subsequent pregnancy
questions.Option_d: expectant mother lacks dietary calcium salts
questions.Explanation: Maternal sensitization during the first Rh+ birth causes production of anti-Rh (anti-D) IgG antibodies that cross the placenta in subsequent Rh+ pregnancies, lysing fetal red blood cells.

questions.Subject: Biology
questions.Question: Systolic blood pressure represents the arterial pressure during
questions.OptionB: atrial filling while all semilunar valves are closed
questions.Option_b: atrial filling while all semilunar valves are closed
questions.Explanation: Systole is the phase of cardiac muscle contraction; peak pressure generated in the brachial artery during ventricular ejection is systolic pressure (~120 mmHg in healthy adults).

questions.Subject: Biology
questions.Question: The functional and structural unit of the nervous system is the
questions.Explanation: Neurons are excitable cells specialized for generating, transmitting, and conducting electrical electrochemical impulses across the nervous system.

questions.Subject: Biology
questions.Question: Which part of a typical motor neuron conducts electrical impulses toward the cell body (soma)?
questions.Explanation: Dendrites are branching cytoplasmic extensions that receive signals from other neurons or receptors and conduct them toward the cell body.

questions.Subject: Biology
questions.Question: The long cylindrical cytoplasmic process that transmits nerve impulses away from the neuron cell body is called the
questions.Explanation: The axon is a single elongated fiber that carries nerve action potentials away from the soma to terminal synaptic knobs.

questions.Subject: Biology
questions.Question: The microscopic junction or gap across which a nerve impulse is chemically transmitted from one neuron to the next is a
questions.Explanation: A synapse is the specialized intercellular junction where neurotransmitter chemicals (e.g. acetylcholine) diffuse across the synaptic cleft from presynaptic to postsynaptic membranes.

questions.Subject: Biology
questions.Question: The Central Nervous System (CNS) in vertebrates consists of the
questions.Explanation: The central nervous system comprises the encephalon (brain) enclosed in the cranium and the spinal cord protected within the vertebral column.

questions.Subject: Biology
questions.Question: Which part of the human brain coordinates voluntary muscular movements, posture, and balance?
questions.Explanation: The cerebellum processes vestibular, proprioceptive, and motor inputs to fine-tune skeletal muscle coordination, posture, and equilibrium.

questions.Subject: Biology
questions.Question: The largest and most developed part of the human brain, responsible for intelligence, memory, thought, and voluntary actions, is the
questions.Explanation: The cerebrum (cerebral cortex) governs conscious thought, intellectual cognition, voluntary motor planning, speech, and sensory perception.

questions.Subject: Biology
questions.Question: The medulla oblongata controls vital involuntary autonomic reflex functions including
questions.OptionA: conscious memory recall and mathematical calculations
questions.OptionB: learning to balance on a bicycle
questions.OptionC: visual perception of distant colour patterns
questions.OptionD: heart rate, breathing (respiration), and blood pressure
questions.Option_a: conscious memory recall and mathematical calculations
questions.Option_b: learning to balance on a bicycle
questions.Option_c: visual perception of distant colour patterns
questions.Option_d: heart rate, breathing (respiration), and blood pressure
questions.Explanation: The brainstem's medulla oblongata houses cardiovascular, vasomotor, and respiratory reflex centers controlling vital involuntary activities.

questions.Subject: Biology
questions.Question: A reflex action is best defined as a
questions.OptionA: rapid, automatic, and involuntary response to a specific stimulus without conscious intervention
questions.OptionB: slow, deliberate calculation performed by the cerebral cortex
questions.OptionC: learned athletic performance achieved through decades of training
questions.OptionD: permanent structural modification of bone joints
questions.Option_a: rapid, automatic, and involuntary response to a specific stimulus without conscious intervention
questions.Option_b: slow, deliberate calculation performed by the cerebral cortex
questions.Option_c: learned athletic performance achieved through decades of training
questions.Option_d: permanent structural modification of bone joints
questions.Explanation: Reflex actions are immediate, protective, involuntary motor responses mediated by neural circuits without waiting for conscious cortical processing.

questions.Subject: Biology
questions.Question: Which of the following is an example of a simple involuntary reflex action?
questions.OptionB: Blinking when an insect flies near the eye
questions.OptionC: Choosing which shirt to wear to a party
questions.OptionD: Writing an essay on civic rights
questions.Option_b: Blinking when an insect flies near the eye
questions.Option_c: Choosing which shirt to wear to a party
questions.Option_d: Writing an essay on civic rights
questions.Explanation: Blinking (corneal reflex), knee-jerk, and pulling the hand from a hot object are rapid protective reflex actions protecting the organism from injury.

questions.Subject: Biology
questions.Question: The anatomical neural pathway followed by nerve impulses during a reflex action is the
questions.Explanation: The reflex arc is the dedicated circuit comprising: receptor → sensory neuron → relay (interneuron) in spinal cord → motor neuron → effector.

questions.Subject: Biology
questions.Question: Which of the following represents the correct sequential path of an impulse across a spinal reflex arc?
questions.OptionA: Effector → Motor neuron → Relay neuron → Sensory neuron → Receptor
questions.OptionB: Receptor → Motor neuron → Brain → Sensory neuron → Effector
questions.OptionC: Sensory neuron → Receptor → Effector → Motor neuron → Relay neuron
questions.OptionD: Receptor → Sensory neuron → Intermediate (relay) neuron → Motor neuron → Effector
questions.Option_a: Effector → Motor neuron → Relay neuron → Sensory neuron → Receptor
questions.Option_b: Receptor → Motor neuron → Brain → Sensory neuron → Effector
questions.Option_c: Sensory neuron → Receptor → Effector → Motor neuron → Relay neuron
questions.Option_d: Receptor → Sensory neuron → Intermediate (relay) neuron → Motor neuron → Effector
questions.Explanation: Sensory receptors detect stimuli; impulses travel via sensory afferents to spinal cord interneurons, which trigger motor efferents delivering commands to effectors.

questions.Subject: Biology
questions.Question: In the mammalian nervous system, the fatty insulating layer that encloses axons and speeds up impulse transmission is the
questions.Explanation: Myelin sheaths formed by Schwann cells insulate axons; action potentials jump between unmyelinated nodes of Ranvier (saltatory conduction), accelerating speed.

questions.Subject: Biology
questions.Question: The autonomic nervous system is subdivided into two anatomically and functionally opposing branches named the
questions.Explanation: The autonomic system regulates involuntary organs via the sympathetic branch ('fight or flight') and parasympathetic branch ('rest and digest').

questions.Subject: Biology
questions.Question: Activation of the sympathetic nervous system produces which physiological response?
questions.OptionA: Constriction of pupils, slowed heart rate, and stimulated digestion
questions.OptionB: Excessive production of saliva and digestive enzymes
questions.OptionC: Dilation of pupils, increased heart rate, and inhibition of digestion
questions.OptionD: Immediate onset of deep biological sleep
questions.Option_a: Constriction of pupils, slowed heart rate, and stimulated digestion
questions.Option_b: Excessive production of saliva and digestive enzymes
questions.Option_c: Dilation of pupils, increased heart rate, and inhibition of digestion
questions.Option_d: Immediate onset of deep biological sleep
questions.Explanation: Sympathetic stimulation prepares the body for emergencies: adrenaline surges, cardiac output increases, bronchioles dilate, and gut motility drops.

questions.Subject: Biology
questions.Question: What chemical neurotransmitter is released into neuromuscular junctions to stimulate skeletal muscle contraction?
questions.Explanation: Acetylcholine (ACh) is released from motor axon terminals, binds nicotinic receptors on the sarcolemma, and depolarizes muscle fibers to trigger contraction.

questions.Subject: Biology
questions.Question: Conditioned reflexes differ from simple inborn reflexes because conditioned reflexes are
questions.OptionA: acquired through learning, experience, and repetitive association (e.g. Pavlov's experiment)
questions.OptionB: present from birth in all members of a species without prior training
questions.OptionC: controlled entirely by the peripheral autonomic ganglia
questions.OptionD: transmitted without involving electrical action potentials
questions.Option_a: acquired through learning, experience, and repetitive association (e.g. Pavlov's experiment)
questions.Option_b: present from birth in all members of a species without prior training
questions.Option_c: controlled entirely by the peripheral autonomic ganglia
questions.Option_d: transmitted without involving electrical action potentials
questions.Explanation: Conditioned reflexes (demonstrated by Ivan Pavlov's dogs salivating at a bell) are learned behaviors established by pairing an unconditioned stimulus with a neutral stimulus.

questions.Subject: Biology
questions.Question: The photoreceptor cells in the human retina responsible for vision in dim light and detecting black-and-white shades are
questions.Explanation: Rods contain the visual pigment rhodopsin, are highly sensitive to low photon levels, and mediate scotopic (night and monochrome) vision.

questions.Subject: Biology
questions.Question: Cones are retinal photoreceptor cells that function optimally in
questions.OptionA: complete darkness to detect auditory sound waves
questions.OptionB: regulating the hydrostatic pressure of the aqueous humor
questions.OptionC: bright light and are responsible for high-acuity colour vision
questions.OptionD: producing tears to lubricate the conjunctival sac
questions.Option_a: complete darkness to detect auditory sound waves
questions.Option_b: regulating the hydrostatic pressure of the aqueous humor
questions.Option_c: bright light and are responsible for high-acuity colour vision
questions.Option_d: producing tears to lubricate the conjunctival sac
questions.Explanation: Cones contain photopsin pigments sensitive to red, green, and blue wavelengths, providing trichromatic daylight vision and fine spatial resolution at the fovea.

questions.Subject: Biology
questions.Question: The yellow spot (fovea centralis) of the retina is the area of greatest visual acuity because it contains
questions.OptionA: only rod cells and extensive blood vessels
questions.OptionB: the exit point of the optic nerve without photoreceptors
questions.OptionC: thick layers of black melanin pigment granules
questions.OptionD: the highest concentration of cone cells and no rod cells
questions.Option_a: only rod cells and extensive blood vessels
questions.Option_b: the exit point of the optic nerve without photoreceptors
questions.Option_c: thick layers of black melanin pigment granules
questions.Option_d: the highest concentration of cone cells and no rod cells
questions.Explanation: The fovea is a tiny central retinal depression densely packed with cones and devoid of rods, providing the sharpest visual acuity.

questions.Subject: Biology
questions.Question: The blind spot in the vertebrate eye is the region where
questions.OptionA: the optic nerve leaves the eyeball, containing no photoreceptors (rods or cones)
questions.OptionB: cataracts accumulate across the crystalline lens
questions.OptionD: ciliary muscles tear during intense reading
questions.Option_a: the optic nerve leaves the eyeball, containing no photoreceptors (rods or cones)
questions.Option_b: cataracts accumulate across the crystalline lens
questions.Option_d: ciliary muscles tear during intense reading
questions.Explanation: At the optic disc (blind spot), ganglion cell axons bundle to form the optic nerve and retinal blood vessels exit; no photoreceptors exist here.

questions.Subject: Biology
questions.Question: Accommodation in the human eye refers to the ability to
questions.OptionA: dilates the pupil in extreme darkness
questions.OptionB: alter the curvature and focal length of the crystalline lens to focus near and distant objects sharply
questions.OptionC: secrete tears to flush out airborne grit
questions.OptionD: move the eyeball rapidly inside the orbital cavity
questions.Option_a: dilates the pupil in extreme darkness
questions.Option_b: alter the curvature and focal length of the crystalline lens to focus near and distant objects sharply
questions.Option_c: secrete tears to flush out airborne grit
questions.Option_d: move the eyeball rapidly inside the orbital cavity
questions.Explanation: Accommodation is the reflex alteration of lens convexity mediated by ciliary muscle contraction and suspensory ligament tension to focus light on the retina.

questions.Subject: Biology
questions.Question: When viewing a nearby object, what changes occur in the ciliary muscles, suspensory ligaments, and lens?
questions.OptionA: Ciliary muscles relax; suspensory ligaments tighten; lens flattens
questions.OptionB: Ciliary muscles and ligaments remain unchanged while the cornea thickens
questions.OptionC: Ciliary muscles contract; suspensory ligaments slacken; lens becomes rounder and more convex
questions.OptionD: The eyeball lengthens physically by two centimeters
questions.Option_a: Ciliary muscles relax; suspensory ligaments tighten; lens flattens
questions.Option_b: Ciliary muscles and ligaments remain unchanged while the cornea thickens
questions.Option_c: Ciliary muscles contract; suspensory ligaments slacken; lens becomes rounder and more convex
questions.Option_d: The eyeball lengthens physically by two centimeters
questions.Explanation: For near vision, ciliary muscles contract, releasing tension on suspensory ligaments, allowing the elastic lens to bulge into a more convex shape.

questions.Subject: Biology
questions.Question: Myopia (short-sightedness) is an eye defect in which parallel light rays from distant objects are focused
questions.OptionA: behind the retina; corrected using convex (converging) lenses
questions.OptionB: directly on the fovea centralis without distortion
questions.OptionC: unequally in different meridians; corrected using cylindrical lenses
questions.OptionD: in front of the retina; corrected using concave (diverging) lenses
questions.Option_a: behind the retina; corrected using convex (converging) lenses
questions.Option_b: directly on the fovea centralis without distortion
questions.Option_c: unequally in different meridians; corrected using cylindrical lenses
questions.Option_d: in front of the retina; corrected using concave (diverging) lenses
questions.Explanation: In myopia (due to an elongated eyeball or overly convex lens), distant images form in front of the retina; diverging concave lenses correct it.

questions.Subject: Biology
questions.Question: Hypermetropia (long-sightedness) is an eye defect where light rays from nearby objects focus behind the retina. It is corrected by wearing
questions.Explanation: In hypermetropia (short eyeball or weak lens), close rays converge behind the retina; convex lenses provide extra converging power to focus images on the retina.

questions.Subject: Biology
questions.Question: Astigmatism is caused by an irregular curvature of the cornea or lens and is corrected by using
questions.Explanation: Astigmatism arises when the cornea is shaped unevenly like a rugby ball rather than spherical; cylindrical lenses compensate for the uneven focal planes.

questions.Subject: Biology
questions.Question: Cataract is an eye condition characterized by the
questions.OptionA: excessive build-up of aqueous humor causing high intraocular pressure
questions.OptionB: detachment of the sensory retina from the vascular choroid
questions.OptionC: clouding or opacity of the crystalline lens, impairing vision
questions.OptionD: bacterial infection of the outer conjunctival mucous membrane
questions.Option_a: excessive build-up of aqueous humor causing high intraocular pressure
questions.Option_b: detachment of the sensory retina from the vascular choroid
questions.Option_c: clouding or opacity of the crystalline lens, impairing vision
questions.Option_d: bacterial infection of the outer conjunctival mucous membrane
questions.Explanation: Cataracts involve progressive protein cross-linking and opacification of the lens, obstructing light transmission to the retina.

questions.Subject: Biology
questions.Question: The middle ear contains three tiny articulating auditory ossicles named
questions.Explanation: The auditory ossicles (malleus, incus, and stapes) bridge the tympanic membrane to the oval window, mechanically amplifying sound vibrations.

questions.Subject: Biology
questions.Question: Which part of the mammalian inner ear is the sensory organ for hearing?
questions.Explanation: The snail-shaped cochlea contains the organ of Corti with sensory hair cells that transduce fluid pressure waves into electrical auditory impulses.

questions.Subject: Biology
questions.Question: The semicircular canals of the inner ear are responsible for maintaining
questions.OptionA: constant atmospheric pressure across the eardrum
questions.OptionB: balance and equilibrium during dynamic angular head movements
questions.OptionC: production of protective earwax in the meatus
questions.Option_a: constant atmospheric pressure across the eardrum
questions.Option_b: balance and equilibrium during dynamic angular head movements
questions.Option_c: production of protective earwax in the meatus
questions.Explanation: Three mutually perpendicular semicircular canals house endolymph and ampullary cristae that detect rotational acceleration to maintain dynamic equilibrium.

questions.Subject: Biology
questions.Question: The Eustachian tube connects the middle ear cavity to the pharynx in order to
questions.OptionA: drain excess tears into the nasal cavity
questions.OptionB: prevent bacterial microbes from entering the oral cavity
questions.OptionC: equalize air pressure on both sides of the tympanic membrane (eardrum)
questions.OptionD: conduct acoustic sound vibrations to the cochlear nerve
questions.Option_a: drain excess tears into the nasal cavity
questions.Option_b: prevent bacterial microbes from entering the oral cavity
questions.Option_c: equalize air pressure on both sides of the tympanic membrane (eardrum)
questions.Option_d: conduct acoustic sound vibrations to the cochlear nerve
questions.Explanation: Swallowing or yawning opens the Eustachian tube, equalizing air pressure between the middle ear cavity and the outside atmosphere to protect the eardrum.

questions.Subject: Biology
questions.Question: Which layer of the mammalian skin contains sensory receptors, blood vessels, sweat glands, and hair follicles?
questions.Explanation: The dermis is the vascular connective tissue layer beneath the epidermis housing tactile Meissner corpuscles, Pacinian corpuscles, sebaceous glands, and hair follicles.

questions.Subject: Biology
questions.Question: Pacinian corpuscles located deep in the dermis and subcutaneous tissues are specialized sensory receptors for detecting
questions.Explanation: Pacinian (lamellar) corpuscles consist of concentric cellular lamellae wrapping a sensory nerve ending, tuned to detect mechanical pressure and vibration.

questions.Subject: Biology
questions.Question: How does the mammalian skin help lower body temperature on a hot afternoon?
questions.OptionA: Vasoconstriction of dermal arterioles and shivering of arrector pili muscles
questions.OptionB: Vasodilation of dermal arterioles and evaporation of sweat from the surface
questions.OptionC: Erection of hair shafts to trap a thick layer of insulating air
questions.OptionD: Cessation of all cellular respiration in subcutaneous adipose tissue
questions.Option_a: Vasoconstriction of dermal arterioles and shivering of arrector pili muscles
questions.Option_b: Vasodilation of dermal arterioles and evaporation of sweat from the surface
questions.Option_c: Erection of hair shafts to trap a thick layer of insulating air
questions.Option_d: Cessation of all cellular respiration in subcutaneous adipose tissue
questions.Explanation: Heat loss is achieved through cutaneous vasodilation (bringing blood near the skin surface) and sweat gland secretion (latent heat of vaporization cools skin).

questions.Subject: Biology
questions.Question: Endocrine glands are known as ductless glands because they secrete their chemical messengers (hormones) directly into the
questions.Explanation: Endocrine glands lack excretory ducts and release hormones directly into capillary blood for systemic transport to target receptors.

questions.Subject: Biology
questions.Question: Which endocrine gland is referred to as the 'master gland' because its secretions regulate the activities of other endocrine glands?
questions.Explanation: The anterior pituitary gland secretes tropic hormones (TSH, ACTH, FSH, LH) that regulate the thyroid, adrenal cortex, and gonads.

questions.Subject: Biology
questions.Question: The hormone insulin is secreted by beta cells of the islets of Langerhans in the pancreas to
questions.OptionA: lower blood glucose levels by promoting cellular uptake and glycogen synthesis
questions.OptionB: raise blood glucose levels by breaking down liver glycogen
questions.OptionC: stimulate gastric glands to secrete hydrochloric acid
questions.OptionD: contract the smooth muscles of the gall bladder
questions.Option_a: lower blood glucose levels by promoting cellular uptake and glycogen synthesis
questions.Option_b: raise blood glucose levels by breaking down liver glycogen
questions.Option_c: stimulate gastric glands to secrete hydrochloric acid
questions.Option_d: contract the smooth muscles of the gall bladder
questions.Explanation: Insulin promotes glucose uptake into skeletal muscles and stimulates glycogenesis in the liver, keeping blood glucose within 70-110 mg/dL.

questions.Subject: Biology
questions.Question: Glucagon is an antagonistic hormone to insulin that acts to
questions.OptionA: decrease blood pressure during cardiovascular shock
questions.OptionB: increase blood glucose concentration by stimulating glycogenolysis in the liver
questions.OptionC: convert glucose into insoluble starch granules in adipose cells
questions.OptionD: inhibit water reabsorption in the renal distal tubules
questions.Option_a: decrease blood pressure during cardiovascular shock
questions.Option_b: increase blood glucose concentration by stimulating glycogenolysis in the liver
questions.Option_c: convert glucose into insoluble starch granules in adipose cells
questions.Option_d: inhibit water reabsorption in the renal distal tubules
questions.Explanation: Secreted by pancreatic alpha cells during hypoglycemia, glucagon stimulates glycogen breakdown (glycogenolysis) and gluconeogenesis in the liver.

questions.Subject: Biology
questions.Question: Adrenaline (epinephrine), the 'fight or flight' hormone, is secreted in response to stress and danger by the
questions.Explanation: The adrenal medulla releases adrenaline in acute stress, accelerating heart rate, elevating blood sugar, dilating bronchioles, and diverting blood to muscles.

questions.Subject: Biology
questions.Question: Thyroxine, an iodine-containing hormone that regulates basal metabolic rate and physical/mental growth, is produced by the
questions.Explanation: The thyroid gland synthesizes thyroxine (T4) and triiodothyronine (T3), which stimulate cellular oxygen consumption and protein synthesis.

questions.Subject: Biology
questions.Question: Deficiency of iodine in the human diet prevents the synthesis of thyroxine, resulting in the enlargement of the neck known as
questions.Explanation: Without dietary iodine, thyroxine levels drop; negative feedback triggers high TSH secretion, stimulating abnormal proliferation of thyroid tissue (goitre).

questions.Subject: Biology
questions.Question: In amphibians, which hormone is indispensable for triggering the metamorphosis of an aquatic tadpole into an adult terrestrial frog?
questions.Explanation: Thyroid hormones (thyroxine) orchestrate amphibian metamorphosis, including the resorption of the tail, development of legs, and restructuring of lungs.

questions.Subject: Biology
questions.Question: The master coordinator linking the nervous system to the endocrine system via the pituitary gland is the
questions.Explanation: The hypothalamus integrates neural cues and secretes releasing and inhibiting neurohormones into hypophyseal portal vessels to control pituitary function.

questions.Subject: Biology
questions.Question: Which hormone stimulates the reabsorption of sodium ions and excretion of potassium ions in the distal tubules of mammalian kidneys?
questions.Explanation: Aldosterone, a mineralocorticoid secreted by the adrenal cortex, regulates electrolyte and water balance by promoting renal Na+ retention and K+ loss.

questions.Subject: Biology
questions.Question: Negative feedback in homeostatic regulation means that an increase in a physiological parameter triggers a response that
questions.OptionA: reverses the deviation and returns the parameter to its normal set-point
questions.OptionB: amplifies the deviation continuously until tissues rupture
questions.OptionC: destroys the receptor cells monitoring the change
questions.OptionD: permanently halts blood circulation through the kidneys
questions.Option_a: reverses the deviation and returns the parameter to its normal set-point
questions.Option_b: amplifies the deviation continuously until tissues rupture
questions.Option_c: destroys the receptor cells monitoring the change
questions.Option_d: permanently halts blood circulation through the kidneys
questions.Explanation: Negative feedback counteracts deviations from homeostatic set-points; when a factor rises or falls, mechanisms are engaged to restore baseline balance.

questions.Subject: Biology
questions.Question: Plant hormones (phytohormones) differ from animal hormones because plant hormones
questions.OptionA: are transported exclusively inside white blood cells
questions.OptionB: are produced in growing apical meristem tissues rather than specialized ductless glands
questions.OptionC: act only on dead sclerenchyma fiber walls
questions.OptionD: are composed exclusively of inorganic calcium salts
questions.Option_a: are transported exclusively inside white blood cells
questions.Option_b: are produced in growing apical meristem tissues rather than specialized ductless glands
questions.Option_c: act only on dead sclerenchyma fiber walls
questions.Option_d: are composed exclusively of inorganic calcium salts
questions.Explanation: Plants lack specialized glands; phytohormones (auxins, gibberellins, cytokinins) are synthesized by growing meristems and diffuse through tissues or vascular strands.

questions.Subject: Biology
questions.Question: Auxin (Indole-3-acetic acid or IAA) promotes phototropism in green shoots because light causes auxin to
questions.OptionA: evaporate completely from the illuminated tip
questions.OptionB: crystallize into insoluble starch reserves in the cortex
questions.OptionC: migrate to the shaded side of the shoot, accelerating cell elongation on that side and bending the shoot toward light
questions.OptionD: inhibit all cell division along the apical meristem
questions.Option_a: evaporate completely from the illuminated tip
questions.Option_b: crystallize into insoluble starch reserves in the cortex
questions.Option_c: migrate to the shaded side of the shoot, accelerating cell elongation on that side and bending the shoot toward light
questions.Option_d: inhibit all cell division along the apical meristem
questions.Explanation: Auxin is photo-sensitive and redistributes to the shaded flank of a stem, stimulating expansin proteins that loosen cell walls and cause asymmetric elongation.

questions.Subject: Biology
questions.Question: Which plant hormone is responsible for breaking seed dormancy and promoting stem elongation and bolting in dwarf plants?
questions.Explanation: Gibberellins stimulate hydrolytic enzyme synthesis (e.g. alpha-amylase in germinating barley) and promote internodal cell elongation.

questions.Subject: Biology
questions.Question: The gaseous plant hormone that promotes the ripening of fleshy fruits and leaf abscission is
questions.Explanation: Ethylene is a volatile hydrocarbon gas (C2H4) that stimulates fruit ripening, chlorophyll degradation, fruit softening, and abscission zone formation.
